segs.e: Linked Discourses 22.1
1. Nakula’s Father
Nakula’s Father
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood.

segs.p: Atha kho nakulapitā gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho nakulapitā gahapati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Nakula’s father went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Ahamasmi, bhante, jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto āturakāyo abhikkhaṇātaṅko.
segs.e: “Sir, I’m an old man, elderly and senior. I’m advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life. My body is ailing and I’m constantly unwell.

segs.p: Aniccadassāvī kho panāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato manobhāvanīyānañca bhikkhūnaṁ.
segs.e: I hardly ever get to see the esteemed mendicants.
May the Buddha please advise me
and instruct me.
It will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.”
“That’s so true, householder! That’s so true, householder!

segs.p: Āturo hāyaṁ, gahapati, kāyo aṇḍabhūto pariyonaddho.
segs.e: For this body is ailing, swaddled in its shell.

segs.p: Yo hi, gahapati, imaṁ kāyaṁ pariharanto muhuttampi ārogyaṁ paṭijāneyya, kimaññatra bālyā?
segs.e: If anyone dragging around this body claimed to be healthy even for an hour, what is that but foolishness?
So you should train like this:
‘Though my body is ailing, my mind will be healthy.’
That’s how you should train.”

segs.p: Atha kho nakulapitā gahapati bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho nakulapitaraṁ gahapatiṁ āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
segs.e: And then the householder Nakula’s father approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he went up to Venerable Sāriputta, bowed, and sat down to one side. Sāriputta said to him:
“Householder, your faculties are so very clear,
and your complexion is pure and bright.

segs.p: Alattha no ajja bhagavato sammukhā dhammiṁ kathaṁ savanāyā”ti?
segs.e: Did you get to hear a Dhamma talk in the Buddha’s presence today?”
“What else, sir, could it be?

segs.p: Idānāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya amatena abhisitto”ti.
segs.e: Just now the Buddha anointed me with the deathless ambrosia of a Dhamma talk.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, gahapati, bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya amatena abhisitto”ti?
segs.e: “But with what kind of ambrosial Dhamma talk did the Buddha anoint you?”

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhante, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁ. Ekamantaṁ nisinno khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ etadavocaṁ:
segs.e: So Nakula’s father told Sāriputta all that had happened, and said,

segs.p: ‘ahamasmi, bhante, jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto āturakāyo abhikkhaṇātaṅko.
Aniccadassāvī kho panāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato manobhāvanīyānañca bhikkhūnaṁ.
Evaṁ vutte, maṁ, bhante, bhagavā etadavoca:
Āturo hāyaṁ, gahapati, kāyo aṇḍabhūto pariyonaddho.
Yo hi, gahapati, imaṁ kāyaṁ pariharanto muhuttampi ārogyaṁ paṭijāneyya, kimaññatra bālyā?
āturakāyassa me sato cittaṁ anāturaṁ bhavissatīti.
Evaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya amatena abhisitto”ti.
segs.e: “That’s the ambrosial Dhamma talk with which I was anointed by the Buddha.”

segs.p: “Na hi pana taṁ, gahapati, paṭibhāsi bhagavantaṁ uttariṁ paṭipucchituṁ:
segs.e: “But didn’t you feel the need to ask the Buddha the further question:

segs.p: ‘kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, āturakāyo ceva hoti āturacitto ca, kittāvatā ca pana āturakāyo hi kho hoti no ca āturacitto’”ti?
segs.e: ‘Sir, how do you define someone ailing in body and ailing in mind, and someone ailing in body and healthy in mind’?”

segs.p: “Dūratopi kho mayaṁ, bhante, āgaccheyyāma āyasmato sāriputtassa santike etassa bhāsitassa atthamaññātuṁ.
segs.e: “Sir, we would travel a long way to learn the meaning of this statement in the presence of Venerable Sāriputta.

segs.p: Sādhu vatāyasmantaṁyeva sāriputtaṁ paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho”ti.
segs.e: May Venerable Sāriputta himself please clarify the meaning of this.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, gahapati, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, householder, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho nakulapitā gahapati āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Nakula’s father.
Sāriputta said this:

segs.p: “Kathañca, gahapati, āturakāyo ceva hoti, āturacitto ca?
segs.e: “And how is one ailing in body and ailing in mind?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto
segs.e: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the qualities of a noble one. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the qualities of a true person.

segs.p: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
They’re obsessed with the thought: ‘I am form, form is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ rūpaṁ, mama rūpan’ti pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino taṁ rūpaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: But that form of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Vedanaṁ attato samanupassati, vedanāvantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā vedanaṁ, vedanāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard feeling as self, self as having feeling, feeling in self, or self in feeling.
They’re obsessed with the thought: ‘I am feeling, feeling is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ vedanā, mama vedanā’ti pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, sā vedanā vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: But that feeling of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Saññaṁ attato samanupassati, saññāvantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā saññaṁ, saññāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard perception as self, self as having perception, perception in self, or self in perception.
They’re obsessed with the thought: ‘I am perception, perception is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ saññā, mama saññā’ti pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, sā saññā vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: But that perception of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Saṅkhāre attato samanupassati, saṅkhāravantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā saṅkhāre, saṅkhāresu vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard choices as self, self as having choices, choices in self, or self in choices.
They’re obsessed with the thought: ‘I am choices, choices are mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ saṅkhārā, mama saṅkhārā’ti pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, te saṅkhārā vipariṇamanti aññathā honti.
segs.e: But those choices of theirs decay and perish,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.
They’re obsessed with the thought: ‘I am consciousness, consciousness is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ viññāṇaṁ, mama viññāṇan’ti pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, taṁ viññāṇaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: But that consciousness of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, āturakāyo ceva hoti āturacitto ca.
segs.e: That’s how one is ailing in body and ailing in mind.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapati, āturakāyo hi kho hoti no ca āturacitto?
segs.e: And how is one ailing in body and healthy in mind?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṁ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṁ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto
segs.e: It’s when a learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: ‘Ahaṁ rūpaṁ, mama rūpan’ti na pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They’re not obsessed with the thought: ‘I am form, form is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ rūpaṁ, mama rūpan’ti apariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, taṁ rūpaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: So when that form of theirs decays and perishes,
it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Na vedanaṁ attato samanupassati, na vedanāvantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā vedanaṁ, na vedanāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard feeling as self, self as having feeling, feeling in self, or self in feeling.

segs.p: ‘Ahaṁ vedanā, mama vedanā’ti na pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They’re not obsessed with the thought: ‘I am feeling, feeling is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ vedanā, mama vedanā’ti apariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, sā vedanā vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: So when that feeling of theirs decays and perishes,
it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Na saññaṁ attato samanupassati, na saññāvantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā saññaṁ, na saññāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard perception as self, self as having perception, perception in self, or self in perception.

segs.p: ‘Ahaṁ saññā, mama saññā’ti na pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They’re not obsessed with the thought: ‘I am perception, perception is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ saññā, mama saññā’ti apariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, sā saññā vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: So when that perception of theirs decays and perishes,
it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Na saṅkhāre attato samanupassati, na saṅkhāravantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā saṅkhāre, na saṅkhāresu vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard choices as self, self as having choices, choices in self, or self in choices.

segs.p: ‘Ahaṁ saṅkhārā, mama saṅkhārā’ti na pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They’re not obsessed with the thought: ‘I am choices, choices are mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ saṅkhārā, mama saṅkhārā’ti apariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, te saṅkhārā vipariṇamanti aññathā honti.
segs.e: So when those choices of theirs decay and perish,
it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā viññāṇaṁ, na viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: ‘Ahaṁ viññāṇaṁ, mama viññāṇan’ti na pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They’re not obsessed with the thought: ‘I am consciousness, consciousness is mine!’

segs.p: Tassa ‘ahaṁ viññāṇaṁ, mama viññāṇan’ti apariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino, taṁ viññāṇaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: So when that consciousness of theirs decays and perishes,
it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, āturakāyo hoti no ca āturacitto”ti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is ailing in body and healthy in mind.”
That is what Venerable Sāriputta said.

segs.p: Attamano nakulapitā gahapati āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṁ abhinandīti.
segs.e: Satisfied, Nakula’s father approved what Sāriputta said.
Linked Discourses 22.2
1. Nakula’s Father
At Devadaha
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati devadahaṁ nāma sakyānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, where they have a town named Devadaha.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā pacchābhūmagamikā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several mendicants who were heading for the west went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “icchāma mayaṁ, bhante, pacchābhūmaṁ janapadaṁ gantuṁ, pacchābhūme janapade nivāsaṁ kappetun”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, we wish to go to a western land to take up residence there.”
“But mendicants, have you taken leave of Sāriputta?”

segs.p: “Na kho no, bhante, apalokito āyasmā sāriputto”ti.
segs.e: “No, sir, we haven’t.”
“You should take leave of Sāriputta.

segs.p: Sāriputto, bhikkhave, paṇḍito, bhikkhūnaṁ anuggāhako sabrahmacārīnan”ti.
segs.e: He’s astute, and supports his spiritual companions, the mendicants.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato avidūre aññatarasmiṁ eḷagalāgumbe nisinno hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Sāriputta was sitting not far from the Buddha in a clump of golden shower trees.

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: And then those mendicants approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. They got up from their seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right. Then they went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and said to him,

segs.p: “icchāma mayaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, pacchābhūmaṁ janapadaṁ gantuṁ, pacchābhūme janapade nivāsaṁ kappetuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, we wish to go to a western land to take up residence there.
We have taken leave of the Teacher.”
“Reverends, there are those who question a mendicant who has gone abroad—
astute aristocrats, brahmins, householders, and ascetics—
for astute people are inquisitive:

segs.p: ‘kiṁvādī panāyasmantānaṁ satthā kimakkhāyī’ti, kacci vo āyasmantānaṁ dhammā sussutā suggahitā sumanasikatā sūpadhāritā suppaṭividdhā paññāya, yathā byākaramānā āyasmanto vuttavādino ceva bhagavato assatha, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyātha, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākareyyātha, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgaccheyyā”ti?
segs.e: ‘But what does the venerables’ Teacher teach? What does he explain?’ I trust the venerables have properly heard, learned, applied the mind, and remembered the teachings, and penetrated them with wisdom. That way, when answering you will repeat what the Buddha has said and not misrepresent him with an untruth. You will explain in line with the teaching, with no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.”

segs.p: “Dūratopi kho mayaṁ, āvuso, āgaccheyyāma āyasmato sāriputtassa santike etassa bhāsitassa atthamaññātuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend, we would travel a long way to learn the meaning of this statement in the presence of Venerable Sāriputta.

segs.p: Sādhu vatāyasmantaṁyeva sāriputtaṁ paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho”ti.
segs.e: May Venerable Sāriputta himself please clarify the meaning of this.”

segs.p: “Tena hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, reverends, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:
“Reverends, there are those who question a mendicant who has gone abroad—
astute aristocrats, brahmins, householders, and ascetics—
for astute people are inquisitive:
‘But what does the venerables’ Teacher teach? What does he explain?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, āvuso, evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: When questioned like this, reverends, you should answer:
‘Reverend, our Teacher explained the removal of desire and lust.’

segs.p: Evaṁ byākatepi kho, āvuso, assuyeva uttariṁ pañhaṁ pucchitāro—
segs.e: When you answer like this, such astute people may inquire further:
‘But regarding what does the venerables’ teacher explain the removal of desire and lust?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, āvuso, evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: When questioned like this, reverends, you should answer:
‘Our teacher explains the removal of desire and lust for form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness.’

segs.p: Evaṁ byākatepi kho, āvuso, assuyeva uttariṁ pañhaṁ pucchitāro—
segs.e: When you answer like this, such astute people may inquire further:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ panāyasmantānaṁ ādīnavaṁ disvā rūpe chandarāgavinayakkhāyī satthā,
segs.e: ‘But what drawback has he seen that he teaches the removal of desire and lust for form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, āvuso, evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: When questioned like this, reverends, you should answer:

segs.p: ‘rūpe kho, āvuso, avigatarāgassa avigatacchandassa avigatapemassa avigatapipāsassa avigatapariḷāhassa avigatataṇhassa tassa rūpassa vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā.
segs.e: ‘If you’re not free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for form, when that form decays and perishes it gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
If you’re not free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: avigatataṇhassa tesaṁ saṅkhārānaṁ vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā.
Viññāṇe avigatarāgassa avigatacchandassa avigatapemassa avigatapipāsassa avigatapariḷāhassa avigatataṇhassa tassa viññāṇassa vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā.
segs.e: consciousness, when that consciousness decays and perishes it gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho no, āvuso, ādīnavaṁ disvā rūpe chandarāgavinayakkhāyī satthā,
segs.e: This is the drawback our Teacher has seen that he teaches the removal of desire and lust for form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness.’

segs.p: Evaṁ byākatepi kho, āvuso, assuyeva uttariṁ pañhaṁ pucchitāro—
segs.e: When you answer like this, such astute people may inquire further:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ panāyasmantānaṁ ānisaṁsaṁ disvā rūpe chandarāgavinayakkhāyī satthā,
segs.e: ‘But what benefit has he seen that he teaches the removal of desire and lust for form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, āvuso, evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: When questioned like this, reverends, you should answer:

segs.p: ‘rūpe kho, āvuso, vigatarāgassa vigatacchandassa vigatapemassa vigatapipāsassa vigatapariḷāhassa vigatataṇhassa tassa rūpassa vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā nuppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā.
segs.e: ‘If you are rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for form, when that form decays and perishes it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
If you are rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for feeling …
perception …

segs.p: saṅkhāresu vigatarāgassa vigatacchandassa vigatapemassa vigatapipāsassa vigatapariḷāhassa vigatataṇhassa tesaṁ saṅkhārānaṁ vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā nuppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā.
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Viññāṇe vigatarāgassa vigatacchandassa vigatapemassa vigatapipāsassa vigatapariḷāhassa vigatataṇhassa tassa viññāṇassa vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā nuppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā.
segs.e: consciousness, when that consciousness decays and perishes it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho no, āvuso, ānisaṁsaṁ disvā rūpe chandarāgavinayakkhāyī satthā, vedanāya …
segs.e: This is the benefit our Teacher has seen that he teaches the removal of desire and lust for form, feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness.’

segs.p: Akusale cāvuso, dhamme upasampajja viharato diṭṭhe ceva dhamme sukho vihāro abhavissa avighāto anupāyāso apariḷāho, kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā, nayidaṁ bhagavā akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānaṁ vaṇṇeyya.
segs.e: If those who acquired and kept unskillful qualities were to live happily in the present life, free of distress, anguish, and fever; and if, when their body breaks up, after death, they could expect to go to a good place, the Buddha would not praise giving up unskillful qualities.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, āvuso, akusale dhamme upasampajja viharato diṭṭhe ceva dhamme dukkho vihāro savighāto saupāyāso sapariḷāho, kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā, tasmā bhagavā akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānaṁ vaṇṇeti.
segs.e: But since those who acquire and keep unskillful qualities live unhappily in the present life, full of distress, anguish, and fever; and since, when their body breaks up, after death, they can expect to go to a bad place, the Buddha praises giving up unskillful qualities.

segs.p: Kusale cāvuso, dhamme upasampajja viharato diṭṭhe ceva dhamme dukkho vihāro abhavissa savighāto saupāyāso sapariḷāho, kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā, nayidaṁ bhagavā kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadaṁ vaṇṇeyya.
segs.e: If those who embraced and kept skillful qualities were to live unhappily in the present life, full of distress, anguish, and fever; and if, when their body breaks up, after death, they could expect to go to a bad place, the Buddha would not praise embracing skillful qualities.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, āvuso, kusale dhamme upasampajja viharato diṭṭhe ceva dhamme sukho vihāro avighāto anupāyāso apariḷāho, kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā, tasmā bhagavā kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadaṁ vaṇṇetī”ti.
segs.e: But since those who embrace and keep skillful qualities live happily in the present life, free of distress, anguish, and fever; and since, when their body breaks up, after death, they can expect to go to a good place, the Buddha praises embracing skillful qualities.”
That is what Venerable Sāriputta said.

segs.p: Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what Sāriputta said.
Linked Discourses 22.3
1. Nakula’s Father
With Hāliddikāni
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākaccāno avantīsu viharati kuraraghare papāte pabbate.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākaccāna was staying in the land of the Avantis near Kuraraghara on Steep Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho hāliddikāni gahapati yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho hāliddikāni gahapati āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Hāliddikāni went up to Venerable Mahākaccāna, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
“Sir, this was said by the Buddha in the Chapter of the Eights, in ‘The Questions of Māgandiya’:
‘After leaving their bastion to migrate without abode,
a sage doesn’t get close to anyone in town.
Rid of sensual pleasures, not expecting,
they wouldn’t get in arguments with people.’

segs.p: Imassa nu kho, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
segs.e: How should we see the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement?”
“Householder, the form element is a bastion for consciousness.
One whose consciousness is shackled by greed for the form element is called a migrant going from bastion to bastion.
The feeling element is a bastion for consciousness.
One whose consciousness is shackled to greed for the feeling element is called a migrant going from bastion to bastion.
The perception element is a bastion for consciousness.
One whose consciousness is shackled to greed for the perception element is called a migrant going from bastion to bastion.
The choices element is a bastion for consciousness.
One whose consciousness is shackled to greed for the choices element is called a migrant going from bastion to bastion.
That’s how one is a migrant going from  bastion to bastion.
And how is one a migrant with no bastion?

segs.p: Rūpadhātuyā kho, gahapati, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā te tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: The Realized One has given up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for the form element; any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies. He has cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
That’s why the Realized One is called a migrant with no bastion.
The Realized One has given up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for the feeling element …
the perception element …
the choices element …

segs.p: viññāṇadhātuyā kho, gahapati, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā te tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: the consciousness element; any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies. He has cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
That’s why the Realized One is called a migrant with no bastion.
That’s how one is a migrant with no bastion.
And how is one a migrant going from abode to abode?
Shackled to chasing the abodes that are the features of sights, one is called a migrant going from abode to abode.
Shackled to chasing the abodes that are the features of sounds …
smells …
tastes …
touches …
thoughts, one is called a migrant going from abode to abode.
That’s how one is a migrant going from abode to abode.
And how is one a migrant without abode?

segs.p: Rūpanimittaniketavisāravinibandhā kho, gahapati, tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: The Realized One has given up being shackled to chasing the abodes that are the features of  sights. He has cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
That’s why the Realized One is called a migrant without abode.
The Realized One has given up being shackled to chasing the abodes that are the features of sounds …
smells …
tastes …
touches …

segs.p: dhammanimittaniketavisāravinibandhā kho, gahapati, tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: ideas. He has cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
That’s why the Realized One is called a migrant without abode.
That’s how one is a migrant without abode.
And how does one get close to people in town?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ekacco gihīhi saṁsaṭṭho viharati sahanandī sahasokī, sukhitesu sukhito, dukkhitesu dukkhito, uppannesu kiccakaraṇīyesu attanā tesu yogaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: It’s when someone mixes closely with laypeople, sharing their joys and sorrows—happy when they’re happy and sad when they’re sad—and getting themselves involved in their business.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, gāme santhavajāto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how one gets close to people in town.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapati, gāme na santhavajāto hoti?
segs.e: And how does one not get close to people in town?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, bhikkhu gihīhi asaṁsaṭṭho viharati na sahanandī na sahasokī na sukhitesu sukhito na dukkhitesu dukkhito, uppannesu kiccakaraṇīyesu na attanā tesu yogaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t mix closely with laypeople, not sharing their joys and sorrows—not happy when they’re happy or sad when they’re sad—and not getting themselves involved in their business.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, gāme na santhavajāto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how one doesn’t get close to people in town.
And how is one not rid of sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ekacco kāmesu avigatarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho.
segs.e: It’s when someone isn’t rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, kāmehi aritto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how one is not rid of sensual pleasures.
And how is one rid of sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ekacco kāmesu vigatarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho.
segs.e: It’s when someone is rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, kāmehi ritto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how one is rid of sensual pleasures.
And how is one expecting?
It’s when someone thinks:

segs.p: ‘evaṁrūpo siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁvedano siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁsañño siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁsaṅkhāro siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁviññāṇo siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘In the future, may I be of such form, such feeling, such perception, such choices, and such consciousness!’
That’s how one is expecting.
And how is one not expecting?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ekaccassa na evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: It’s when someone doesn’t think:

segs.p: ‘evaṁrūpo siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁvedano siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁsañño siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁsaṅkhāro siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, evaṁviññāṇo siyaṁ anāgatamaddhānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘In the future, may I be of such form, such feeling, such perception, such choices, and such consciousness!’
That’s how one is not expecting.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapati, kathaṁ viggayha janena kattā hoti?
segs.e: And how does one argue with people?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ekacco evarūpiṁ kathaṁ kattā hoti:
segs.e: It’s when someone takes part in this sort of discussion:

segs.p: ‘na tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāsi; ahaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāmi. Kiṁ tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānissasi? Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi; ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Pure vacanīyaṁ pacchā avaca; pacchā vacanīyaṁ pure avaca. Sahitaṁ me, asahitaṁ te. Adhiciṇṇaṁ te viparāvattaṁ. Āropito te vādo; cara vādappamokkhāya. Niggahitosi; nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’ti.
segs.e: ‘You don’t understand this teaching and training. I understand this teaching and training. What, you understand this teaching and training? You’re practicing wrong. I’m practicing right. You said last what you should have said first. You said first what you should have said last. I stay on topic, you don’t. What you’ve thought so much about has been disproved. Your doctrine is refuted. Go on, save your doctrine! You’re trapped; get yourself out of this—if you can!’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, kathaṁ viggayha janena kattā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how one argues with people.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapati, kathaṁ na viggayha janena kattā hoti?
segs.e: And how does one not argue with people?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, bhikkhu na evarūpiṁ kathaṁ kattā hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t take part in this sort of discussion:

segs.p: ‘na tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāsi …pe… nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’ti.
segs.e: ‘You don’t understand this teaching and training … get yourself out of this—if you can!’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, kathaṁ na viggayha janena kattā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how one doesn’t argue with people.

segs.p: Iti kho, gahapati, yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā aṭṭhakavaggiye māgaṇḍiyapañhe:
segs.e: So, householder, that’s how to understand the detailed meaning of what the Buddha said in brief in the Chapter of the Eights, in ‘The Questions of Māgandiya’:
‘After leaving their bastion to migrate without abode,
a sage doesn’t get close to anyone in town.
Rid of sensual pleasures, not expecting,
they wouldn’t get in arguments with people.’”

segs.p: Imassa kho, gahapati, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 22.4
1. Nakula’s Father
Hāliddikāni (2nd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākaccāno avantīsu viharati kuraraghare papāte pabbate.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākaccāna was staying in the land of the Avantis near Kuraraghara on Steep Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho hāliddikāni gahapati yenāyasmā mahākaccāno …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho hāliddikāni gahapati āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Hāliddikāni went up to Venerable Mahākaccāna … and asked him,
“Sir, this was said by the Buddha in ‘The Questions of Sakka’:

segs.p: ‘ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā, te accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemino accantabrahmacārino accantapariyosānā seṭṭhā devamanussānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Those ascetics and brahmins who are freed due to the ending of craving have reached the ultimate goal, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate end, and are best among gods and humans.’

segs.p: Imassa nu kho, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
segs.e: How should we see the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement?”

segs.p: “Rūpadhātuyā kho, gahapati, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, tesaṁ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā ‘cittaṁ suvimuttanti’ vuccati.
segs.e: “Householder, consider any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for the form element; any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies. With the ending, fading away, cessation, giving away, and letting go of that, the mind is said to be ‘well freed’.
Consider any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for the feeling element …
the perception element …
the choices element …

segs.p: viññāṇadhātuyā kho, gahapati, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, tesaṁ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā ‘cittaṁ suvimuttanti’ vuccati.
segs.e: the consciousness element; any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies. With the ending, fading away, cessation, giving away, and letting go of that, the mind is said to be ‘well freed’.

segs.p: Iti kho, gahapati, yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā sakkapañhe:
segs.e: So, householder, that’s how to understand the detailed meaning of what the Buddha said in brief in ‘The Questions of Sakka’:

segs.p: ‘ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā te accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemino accantabrahmacārino accantapariyosānā seṭṭhā devamanussānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Those ascetics and brahmins who are freed due to the ending of craving have reached the ultimate goal, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate end, and are best among gods and humans.’”

segs.p: Imassa kho, gahapati, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 22.5
1. Nakula’s Father
Development of Immersion
So I have heard.
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, develop immersion.
A mendicant who has immersion truly understands.
What do they truly understand?

segs.p: Rūpassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, saññāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, saṅkhārānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, viññāṇassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca.
segs.e: The origin and ending of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Ko ca, bhikkhave, rūpassa samudayo, ko vedanāya samudayo, ko saññāya samudayo, ko saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo, ko viññāṇassa samudayo?
segs.e: And what is the origin of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging.
What do they approve, welcome, and keep clinging to?
They approve, welcome, and keep clinging to form.

segs.p: Tassa rūpaṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: This gives rise to relishing.
Relishing forms is grasping.
Their grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
They approve, welcome, and keep clinging to feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness.

segs.p: Tassa viññāṇaṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: This gives rise to relishing.
Relishing consciousness is grasping.
Their grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a condition that gives rise to old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
This is the origin of form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness.

segs.p: Ko ca, bhikkhave, rūpassa atthaṅgamo, ko vedanāya …
segs.e: And what is the ending of form, feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging.
What don’t they approve, welcome, or keep clinging to?
They don’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging to form.

segs.p: Tassa rūpaṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā rūpe nandī sā nirujjhati.
segs.e: As a result, relishing of form ceases.
When that relishing ceases, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
They don’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging to feeling …

segs.p: Tassa vedanaṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā vedanāya nandī sā nirujjhati.

segs.e: perception …
choices …

segs.p: Tassa saṅkhāre anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā saṅkhāresu nandī sā nirujjhati.

segs.e: consciousness.

segs.p: Tassa viññāṇaṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā viññāṇe nandī sā nirujjhati.
segs.e: As a result, relishing of consciousness ceases.
When that relishing ceases, grasping ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpassa atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ vedanāya atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ saññāya atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti.
segs.e: This is the ending of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.”
Linked Discourses 22.6
1. Nakula’s Father
Retreat
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, meditate in retreat.
A mendicant in retreat truly understands.
What do they truly understand?

segs.p: Rūpassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, saññāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, saṅkhārānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, viññāṇassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca …pe…
segs.e: The origin and disappearance of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. …”
(Tell in full as in the previous discourse.)
Linked Discourses 22.7
1. Nakula’s Father
Anxiety Because of Grasping
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you how grasping leads to anxiety, and how not grasping leads to freedom from anxiety.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti, kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And how does grasping lead to anxiety?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto
segs.e: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ rūpaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: But that form of theirs decays and perishes,
and consciousness latches on to the perishing of form.

segs.p: Tassa rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
segs.e: Anxieties occupy their mind, born of latching on to the perishing of form, and originating in accordance with natural principles.

segs.p: Cetaso pariyādānā uttāsavā ca hoti vighātavā ca apekkhavā ca upādāya ca paritassati.
segs.e: So they become frightened, worried, concerned, and anxious because of grasping.

segs.p: Vedanaṁ attato samanupassati, vedanāvantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā vedanaṁ, vedanāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard feeling as self …

segs.p: Tassa sā vedanā vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
Tassa vedanāvipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
Cetaso pariyādānā uttāsavā ca hoti vighātavā ca apekkhavā ca upādāya ca paritassati.

segs.e: They regard perception as self …

segs.p: saṅkhāre attato samanupassati, saṅkhāravantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā saṅkhāre, saṅkhāresu vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard choices as self …

segs.p: Tassa te saṅkhārā vipariṇamanti aññathā honti.
Tassa saṅkhāravipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
Cetaso pariyādānā uttāsavā ca hoti vighātavā ca apekkhavā ca upādāya ca paritassati.
Viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ viññāṇaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: But that consciousness of theirs decays and perishes,
and consciousness latches on to the perishing of consciousness.

segs.p: Tassa viññāṇavipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
segs.e: Anxieties occupy their mind, born of latching on to the perishing of consciousness, and originating in accordance with natural principles.

segs.p: Cetaso pariyādānā uttāsavā ca hoti vighātavā ca apekkhavā ca upādāya ca paritassati.
segs.e: So they become frightened, worried, concerned, and anxious because of grasping.
That’s how grasping leads to anxiety.
And how does not grasping lead to freedom from anxiety?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṁ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto, sappurisānaṁ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto
segs.e: It’s when a learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ rūpaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: When that form of theirs decays and perishes,

segs.p: Tassa rūpavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā na rūpavipariṇāmānuparivatti viññāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: consciousness doesn’t latch on to the perishing of form.

segs.p: Tassa na rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
segs.e: Anxieties—born of latching on to the perishing of form and originating in accordance with natural principles—don’t occupy their mind.

segs.p: Cetaso apariyādānā na cevuttāsavā hoti na ca vighātavā na ca apekkhavā, anupādāya ca na paritassati.
segs.e: So they don’t become frightened, worried, concerned, or anxious because of grasping.

segs.p: Na vedanaṁ attato samanupassati, na vedanāvantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā vedanaṁ, na vedanāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard feeling as self …

segs.p: Tassa sā vedanā vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
Tassa vedanāvipariṇāmaññathābhāvā na vedanāvipariṇāmānuparivatti viññāṇaṁ hoti.
Tassa na vedanāvipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
Cetaso apariyādānā na cevuttāsavā hoti na ca vighātavā na ca apekkhavā, anupādāya ca na paritassati.
Na saññaṁ …pe… na saṅkhāre attato samanupassati,
segs.e: They don’t regard perception as self …

segs.p: na attani vā saṅkhāre, na saṅkhāresu vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard choices as self …

segs.p: Tassa te saṅkhārā vipariṇamanti aññathā honti.
Tassa saṅkhāravipariṇāmaññathābhāvā na saṅkhāravipariṇāmānuparivatti viññāṇaṁ hoti.
Tassa na saṅkhāravipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
Cetaso apariyādānā na cevuttāsavā hoti na ca vighātavā na ca apekkhavā, anupādāya ca na paritassati.
Na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ …pe…
segs.e: They don’t regard consciousness as self …

segs.p: tassa taṁ viññāṇaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
segs.e: When that consciousness of theirs decays and perishes,

segs.p: Tassa viññāṇavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā na viññāṇavipariṇāmānuparivatti viññāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: consciousness doesn’t latch on to the perishing of consciousness.

segs.p: Tassa na viññāṇavipariṇāmānuparivattijā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
segs.e: Anxieties—born of latching on to the perishing of consciousness and originating in accordance with natural principles—don’t occupy their mind.

segs.p: Cetaso apariyādānā na cevuttāsavā hoti na ca vighātavā na ca apekkhavā, anupādāya ca na paritassati.
segs.e: So they don’t become frightened, worried, concerned, or anxious because of grasping.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, anupādā aparitassanaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how not grasping leads to freedom from anxiety.”

2. Impermanence
Impermanence
So I have heard.
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ, vedanā aniccā, saññā aniccā, saṅkhārā aniccā, viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are impermanent.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

With Ānanda
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of ‘cessation’.

segs.p: Katamesānaṁ kho, bhante, dhammānaṁ nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccatī”ti?
segs.e: The cessation of what things does this refer to?”

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, ānanda, aniccaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ khayadhammaṁ vayadhammaṁ virāgadhammaṁ nirodhadhammaṁ.
segs.e: “Ānanda, form is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.
Its cessation is what ‘cessation’ refers to.

segs.p: Vedanā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā.
segs.e: Feeling …
Perception …

segs.p: saṅkhārā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā.
segs.e: Choices …

segs.p: Viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ khayadhammaṁ vayadhammaṁ virāgadhammaṁ nirodhadhammaṁ.
segs.e: Consciousness is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.
Its cessation is what ‘cessation’ refers to.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṁ nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccatī”ti.
segs.e: When they speak of ‘cessation’, its the cessation of these things that this refers to.”
Linked Discourses 22.22
3. The Burden
The Burden of Responsibility
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “bhārañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi bhārahārañca bhārādānañca bhāranikkhepanañca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you the burden, the bearer of the burden, the taking up of the burden, and the putting down of the burden.
Listen …
And what is the burden?
The five grasping aggregates, it should be said.
What five?
The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
This is called the burden.
And who is the bearer of the burden?
The individual, it should be said;
the venerable of such name and such clan.
This is called the bearer of the burden.
And what is the taking up of the burden?

segs.p: Yāyaṁ taṇhā ponobhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: It’s the craving that leads to future lives, mixed up with relishing and greed, taking pleasure there wherever it alights. That is,
craving for sensual pleasures, craving for continued existence, and craving for nonexistence.
This is called the taking up of the burden.
And what is the putting down of the burden?

segs.p: Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo.
segs.e: It’s the fading away and cessation of that very same craving no residue left behind; giving it away, letting it go, releasing it, and not clinging to it.
This is called the putting down of the burden.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“The five aggregates are indeed burdens,
and the individual is the bearer of the burden.
Taking up the burden is suffering in the world,
and putting the burden down is happiness.
When the heavy burden is put down
without taking up another,
one who has plucked out craving, root and all,
is hungerless, quenched.”
Linked Discourses 22.23
3. The Burden
Complete Understanding
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you the things that should be completely understood, and complete understanding.
Listen …
And what things should be completely understood?

segs.p: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, pariññeyyo dhammo, vedanā pariññeyyo dhammo, saññā pariññeyyo dhammo, saṅkhārā pariññeyyo dhammo, viññāṇaṁ pariññeyyo dhammo.
segs.e: Form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
These are called the things that should be completely understood.
And what is complete understanding?
The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.
This is called complete understanding.”
Linked Discourses 22.24
3. The Burden
Directly Knowing
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya;
segs.e: “Mendicants, without directly knowing and completely understanding form, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.

segs.p: vedanaṁ anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya;
segs.e: Without directly knowing and completely understanding feeling …
perception …

segs.p: saṅkhāre anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya;
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: consciousness, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.

segs.p: Rūpañca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṁ parijānaṁ virājayaṁ pajahaṁ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya;
segs.e: By directly knowing and completely understanding form, having dispassion for it and giving it up, you can end suffering.
By directly knowing and completely understanding feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ abhijānaṁ parijānaṁ virājayaṁ pajahaṁ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti.
segs.e: consciousness, having dispassion for it and giving it up, you can end suffering.”
Linked Discourses 22.25
3. The Burden
Desire and Greed
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, give up desire and greed for form.

segs.p: Evaṁ taṁ rūpaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
segs.e: Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
Give up desire and greed for feeling …

segs.p: Evaṁ sā vedanā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.

segs.e: perception …

segs.p: Evaṁ sā saññā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.

segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Evaṁ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.

segs.e: consciousness.

segs.p: Evaṁ taṁ viññāṇaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhamman”ti.
segs.e: Thus that consciousness will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”
Linked Discourses 22.26
3. The Burden
Gratification
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho rūpassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇaṁ?
segs.e: ‘What’s the gratification, the drawback, and the escape when it comes to form …

segs.p: Ko vedanāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇaṁ?
segs.e: feeling …

segs.p: Ko saññāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇaṁ?
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: Ko saṅkhārānaṁ assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇaṁ?
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Ko viññāṇassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇan’ti?
segs.e: and consciousness?’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho rūpaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ rūpassa assādo.
segs.e: ‘The pleasure and happiness that arise from form: this is its gratification.

segs.p: Yaṁ rūpaṁ aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, ayaṁ rūpassa ādīnavo.
segs.e: That form is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

segs.p: Yo rūpasmiṁ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ rūpassa nissaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Removing and giving up desire and greed for form: this is its escape.

segs.p: Yaṁ vedanaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ vedanāya assādo.
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness that arise from feeling …

segs.p: Yaṁ vedanā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṁ vedanāya ādīnavo.
Yo vedanāya chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ vedanāya nissaraṇaṁ.

segs.e: perception …

segs.p: yaṁ saṅkhāre paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ saṅkhārānaṁ assādo.
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Yaṁ saṅkhārā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṁ saṅkhārānaṁ ādīnavo.
Yo saṅkhāresu chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ saṅkhārānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ.
Yaṁ viññāṇaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ viññāṇassa assādo.
segs.e: consciousness: this is its gratification.

segs.p: Yaṁ viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, ayaṁ viññāṇassa ādīnavo.
segs.e: That consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

segs.p: Yo viññāṇasmiṁ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṁ’.
segs.e: Removing and giving up desire and greed for consciousness: this is its escape.’

segs.p: Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ evaṁ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññāsiṁ, neva tāvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ‘sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṁ.
segs.e: As long as I didn’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape in this way for what they are, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

segs.p: Yato ca khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ evaṁ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ;
segs.e: But when I did truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape in this way for what they are, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

segs.p: athāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṁ.

segs.e: Knowledge and vision arose in me:

segs.p: ‘akuppā me vimutti; ayamantimā jāti; natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”
Linked Discourses 22.27
3. The Burden
Gratification (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I went in search of form’s gratification,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā rūpassa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of form’s gratification.
I went in search of form’s drawback,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā rūpassa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of form’s drawback.
I went in search of form’s escape,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā rūpassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāya me taṁ sudiṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of form’s escape.
I went in search of the gratification of feeling …
perception …
choices …
and consciousness,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā viññāṇassa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of consciousness’s gratification.
I went in search of consciousness’s drawback,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā viññāṇassa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of consciousness’s drawback.
I went in search of consciousness’s escape,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāya me taṁ sudiṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of consciousness’s escape.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññāsiṁ …pe…
segs.e: As long as I didn’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening …
But when I did truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, I announced my supreme perfect awakening …
Knowledge and vision arose in me:

segs.p: ‘akuppā me vimutti; ayamantimā jāti; natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”
Linked Discourses 22.28
3. The Burden
Gratification (3rd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpassa assādo abhavissa nayidaṁ sattā rūpasmiṁ sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, if there were no gratification in form, sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpassa assādo, tasmā sattā rūpasmiṁ sārajjanti.
segs.e: But since there is gratification in form, sentient beings are aroused by it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpassa ādīnavo abhavissa nayidaṁ sattā rūpasmiṁ nibbindeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If form had no drawback, sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpassa ādīnavo, tasmā sattā rūpasmiṁ nibbindanti.
segs.e: But since form has a drawback, sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpassa nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa nayidaṁ sattā rūpasmā nissareyyuṁ.
segs.e: If there were no escape from form, sentient beings wouldn’t escape from it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpassa nissaraṇaṁ, tasmā sattā rūpasmā nissaranti.
segs.e: But since there is an escape from form, sentient beings do escape from it.
If there were no gratification in feeling …
perception …

segs.p: no cedaṁ, bhikkhave, saṅkhārānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā saṅkhārehi nissareyyuṁ.
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi saṅkhārānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ, tasmā sattā saṅkhārehi nissaranti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, viññāṇassa assādo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā viññāṇasmiṁ sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: consciousness, sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi viññāṇassa assādo, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmiṁ sārajjanti.
segs.e: But since there is gratification in consciousness, sentient beings are aroused by it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, viññāṇassa ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā viññāṇasmiṁ nibbindeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If consciousness had no drawback, sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi viññāṇassa ādīnavo, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmiṁ nibbindanti.
segs.e: But since consciousness has a drawback, sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā viññāṇasmā nissareyyuṁ.
segs.e: If there were no escape from consciousness, sentient beings wouldn’t escape from it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṁ, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmā nissaranti.
segs.e: But since there is an escape from consciousness, sentient beings do escape from it.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññaṁsu;
segs.e: As long as sentient beings don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, they haven’t escaped from this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—and they don’t live detached, liberated, with mind free of limits.

segs.p: neva tāva, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaṁyuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā vihariṁsu.
Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññaṁsu;
segs.e: But when sentient beings truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, they’ve escaped from this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—and they live detached, liberated, with mind free of limits.”

segs.p: atha, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaṁyuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharanti”.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 22.29
3. The Burden
Taking Pleasure
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ abhinandati, dukkhaṁ so abhinandati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, if you take pleasure in form, you take pleasure in suffering.

segs.p: Yo dukkhaṁ abhinandati, ‘aparimutto so dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: If you take pleasure in suffering, you’re not free from suffering, I say.
If you take pleasure in feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: yo viññāṇaṁ abhinandati, dukkhaṁ so abhinandati.
segs.e: consciousness, you take pleasure in suffering.

segs.p: Yo dukkhaṁ abhinandati, ‘aparimutto so dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: If you take pleasure in suffering, you’re not free from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ nābhinandati, dukkhaṁ so nābhinandati.
segs.e: If you don’t take pleasure in form, you don’t take pleasure in suffering.

segs.p: Yo dukkhaṁ nābhinandati, ‘parimutto so dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: If you don’t take pleasure in suffering, you’re free from suffering, I say.
If you don’t take pleasure in feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: yo viññāṇaṁ nābhinandati, dukkhaṁ so nābhinandati.
segs.e: consciousness, you don’t take pleasure in suffering.

segs.p: Yo dukkhaṁ nābhinandati, ‘parimutto so dukkhasmā’ti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: If you don’t take pleasure in suffering, you’re free from suffering, I say.”
Linked Discourses 22.30
3. The Burden
Arising
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo rogānaṁ ṭhiti jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of form is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.
The arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: yo viññāṇassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo rogānaṁ ṭhiti jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo.
segs.e: consciousness is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho rogānaṁ vūpasamo jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo.
segs.e: The cessation, settling, and disappearance of form is the cessation of suffering, the settling of diseases, and the disappearance of old age and death.
The cessation, settling, and disappearance of feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: yo viññāṇassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho rogānaṁ vūpasamo jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti.
segs.e: consciousness is the cessation of suffering, the settling of diseases, and the disappearance of old age and death.”
Linked Discourses 22.31
3. The Burden
The Root of Gloom
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you gloom and the root of gloom.
Listen …
And what is gloom?

segs.p: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, aghaṁ, vedanā aghaṁ, saññā aghaṁ, saṅkhārā aghaṁ, viññāṇaṁ aghaṁ.
segs.e: Form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are gloom.
This is called gloom.
And what is the root of gloom?
It’s the craving that leads to future lives, mixed up with relishing and greed, taking pleasure there wherever it alights. That is,
craving for sensual pleasures, craving for continued existence, and craving for nonexistence.
This is called the root of gloom.”
Linked Discourses 22.32
3. The Burden
Brittle
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you what is brittle and what is not brittle.
Listen …
And what is brittle? What is not brittle?
Form is brittle,

segs.p: Yo tassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, idaṁ appabhaṅgu.
segs.e: but its cessation, settling, and disappearance is not brittle.
Feeling …

segs.p: Yo tassā nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, idaṁ appabhaṅgu.

segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.
And what isn’t yours?

segs.p: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṁ, taṁ pajahatha.
segs.e: Form isn’t yours: give it up.

At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu;
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho, appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
“Yaṁ kho, bhikkhu, anuseti, tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati;
segs.e: “Mendicant, you’re reckoned by what you have an underlying tendency for.

segs.p: yaṁ nānuseti, na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: You’re not reckoned by what you have no underlying tendency for.”
“Understood, Blessed One! Understood, Holy One!”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsī”ti?
segs.e: “But how do you see the detailed meaning of my brief statement?”
“If you have an underlying tendency for form, you’re reckoned by that.
If you have an underlying tendency for feeling …
perception …

segs.p: Saṅkhāre ce anuseti tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: choices …
consciousness, you’re reckoned by that.

segs.p: Rūpañce, bhante, nānuseti na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: If you have no underlying tendency for form, you’re not reckoned by that.
If you have no underlying tendency for feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇañce nānuseti na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: consciousness, you’re not reckoned by that.

segs.p: Imassa khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.”
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsi.
segs.e: It’s good that you understand the detailed meaning of what I’ve said in brief like this.

segs.p: Rūpañce, bhikkhu, anuseti tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: If you have an underlying tendency for form, you’re reckoned by that.
If you have an underlying tendency for feeling …

consciousness, you’re reckoned by that.

segs.p: Rūpañce, bhikkhu, nānuseti na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: If you have no underlying tendency for form, you’re not reckoned by that.
If you have no underlying tendency for feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇañce nānuseti na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: consciousness, you’re not reckoned by that.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṅkhittena, bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.
segs.e: This is how to see the detailed meaning of what I said in brief.”

segs.p: Atha kho so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: And then that mendicant approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho so bhikkhu eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then that mendicant, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And that mendicant became one of the perfected.

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: sitting to one side, the Buddha said to him:
“Ānanda, suppose they were to ask you:

segs.p: ‘katamesaṁ, āvuso ānanda, dhammānaṁ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṁ paññāyatī’ti?
segs.e: ‘Reverend Ānanda, what are the things for which arising is evident, vanishing is evident, and change while persisting is evident?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭho tvaṁ, ānanda, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti?

segs.p: ‘rūpassa kho, āvuso, uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṁ paññāyati.
segs.e: ‘Reverend, the arising of form is evident, its vanishing is evident, and change while persisting is evident.

perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṁ paññāyati.
