segs.e: its arising, vanishing, and change while persisting are evident.
Whatever feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness has been born, and has appeared,

segs.p: tassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṁ paññāyati.
segs.e: its arising, vanishing, and change while persisting are evident.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṁ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṁ paññāyatīti.
segs.e: These are the things for which arising is evident, vanishing is evident, and change while persisting is evident.

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭho tvaṁ, ānanda, evaṁ byākareyyāsī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how you should answer such a question.”
Linked Discourses 22.39
4. It’s Not Yours
In Line With the Teaching
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, when a mendicant is practicing in line with the teaching, this is what’s in line with the teaching.

segs.p: yaṁ rūpe nibbidābahulo vihareyya, vedanāya nibbidābahulo vihareyya, saññāya nibbidābahulo vihareyya, saṅkhāresu nibbidābahulo vihareyya, viññāṇe nibbidābahulo vihareyya.
segs.e: They should live full of disillusionment for form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Yo rūpe nibbidābahulo viharanto, vedanāya … saññāya … saṅkhāresu nibbidābahulo viharanto, viññāṇe nibbidābahulo viharanto rūpaṁ parijānāti, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ parijānāti,
segs.e: Living in this way, they completely understand form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: so rūpaṁ parijānaṁ, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ parijānaṁ parimuccati rūpamhā, parimuccati vedanāya, parimuccati saññāya, parimuccati saṅkhārehi, parimuccati viññāṇamhā,
segs.e: Completely understanding form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness, they’re freed from these things.

segs.p: parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re freed from suffering, I say.”
Linked Discourses 22.40
4. It’s Not Yours
In Line With the Teaching (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Dhammānudhammappaṭipannassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ayamanudhammo hoti yaṁ rūpe aniccānupassī vihareyya …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant is practicing in line with the teaching, this is what’s in line with the teaching. They should meditate observing impermanence in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. …
They’re freed from suffering, I say.”
Linked Discourses 22.41
4. It’s Not Yours
In Line With the Teaching (3rd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Dhammānudhammappaṭipannassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ayamanudhammo hoti yaṁ rūpe dukkhānupassī vihareyya …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant is practicing in line with the teaching, this is what’s in line with the teaching. They should meditate observing suffering in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. …
They’re freed from suffering, I say.”
Linked Discourses 22.42
4. It’s Not Yours
In Line With the Teaching (4th)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Dhammānudhammappaṭipannassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ayamanudhammo hoti yaṁ rūpe anattānupassī vihareyya, vedanāya … saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe anattānupassī vihareyya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant is practicing in line with the teaching, this is what’s in line with the teaching. They should meditate observing not-self in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. …

segs.p: Yo rūpe anattānupassī viharanto …pe… rūpaṁ parijānāti, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ parijānāti, so rūpaṁ parijānaṁ, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ parijānaṁ parimuccati rūpamhā, parimuccati vedanāya, parimuccati saññāya, parimuccati saṅkhārehi, parimuccati viññāṇamhā, parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: They’re freed from suffering, I say.”
Linked Discourses 22.43
5. Be Your Own Island
Be Your Own Island
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, be your own island, your own refuge, with no other refuge. Let the teaching be your island and your refuge, with no other refuge.

segs.p: Attadīpānaṁ, bhikkhave, viharataṁ attasaraṇānaṁ anaññasaraṇānaṁ, dhammadīpānaṁ dhammasaraṇānaṁ anaññasaraṇānaṁ yoni upaparikkhitabbā ‘Kiṁjātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, kiṁpahotikā’ti?
segs.e: When you live like this, you should examine rationally: ‘From what are sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress born and produced?’
And, mendicants, from what are sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress born and produced?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto,
segs.e: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ rūpaṁ vipariṇamati, aññathā ca hoti.
segs.e: But that form of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Vedanaṁ attato samanupassati, vedanāvantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā vedanaṁ, vedanāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard feeling as self …

segs.p: Tassa sā vedanā vipariṇamati, aññathā ca hoti.

segs.e: They regard perception as self …
They regard choices as self …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ viññāṇaṁ vipariṇamati, aññathā ca hoti.
segs.e: But that consciousness of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Rūpassa tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṁ viditvā vipariṇāmaṁ virāgaṁ nirodhaṁ, ‘pubbe ceva rūpaṁ etarahi ca sabbaṁ rūpaṁ aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhamman’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: Sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are given up when you understand the impermanence of form—its perishing, fading away, and cessation—and you truly see with right understanding that all form, whether past or present, is impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

segs.p: Tesaṁ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṁ sukhaṁ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccati.
segs.e: When these things are given up there’s no anxiety. Without anxiety you live happily. A mendicant who lives happily is said to be quenched in that respect.

segs.p: Vedanāya tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṁ viditvā vipariṇāmaṁ virāgaṁ nirodhaṁ, ‘pubbe ceva vedanā etarahi ca sabbā vedanā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: Sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are given up when you understand the impermanence of feeling …

segs.p: Tesaṁ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṁ sukhaṁ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccati.

segs.e: perception …

segs.p: saṅkhārānaṁ tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṁ viditvā vipariṇāmaṁ virāgaṁ nirodhaṁ, ‘pubbe ceva saṅkhārā etarahi ca sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Tesaṁ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṁ sukhaṁ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccati.

Viññāṇassa tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṁ viditvā vipariṇāmaṁ virāgaṁ nirodhaṁ, ‘pubbe ceva viññāṇaṁ etarahi ca sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhamman’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: consciousness—its perishing, fading away, and cessation—and you truly see with right understanding that all consciousness, whether past or present, is impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

segs.p: Tesaṁ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṁ sukhaṁ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccatī”ti.
segs.e: When these things are given up there’s no anxiety. Without anxiety you live happily. A mendicant who lives happily is said to be quenched in that respect.”
Linked Discourses 22.44
5. Be Your Own Island
Practice
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Sakkāyasamudayagāminiñca vo, bhikkhave, paṭipadaṁ desessāmi, sakkāyanirodhagāminiñca paṭipadaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you the practice that leads to the origin of substantial reality and the practice that leads to the cessation of substantial reality.
Listen …
And what is the practice that leads to the origin of substantial reality?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto,
segs.e: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
They regard feeling as self …
They regard perception as self …
They regard choices as self …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘sakkāyasamudayagāminī paṭipadā, sakkāyasamudayagāminī paṭipadā’ti.
segs.e: This is called the practice that leads to the origin of substantial reality.
And that’s why it’s called a way of regarding things that leads to the origin of suffering.
And what is the practice that leads to the cessation of substantial reality?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṁ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto, sappurisānaṁ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto,
segs.e: It’s when a learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
They don’t regard feeling as self …
They don’t regard perception as self …
They don’t regard choices as self …

segs.p: na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā viññāṇaṁ, na viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti.
segs.e: This is called the practice that leads to the cessation of substantial reality.
And that’s why it’s called a way of regarding things that leads to the cessation of suffering.”
Linked Discourses 22.45
5. Be Your Own Island
Impermanence
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, form is impermanent.
What’s impermanent is suffering.
What’s suffering is not-self.

segs.p: yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato cittaṁ virajjati vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi.
segs.e: Seeing truly with right understanding like this, the mind becomes dispassionate and freed from defilements by not grasping.
Feeling is impermanent …
Perception …
Choices …
Consciousness is impermanent.
What’s impermanent is suffering.
What’s suffering is not-self.

segs.p: yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato cittaṁ virajjati vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi.
segs.e: Seeing truly with right understanding like this, the mind becomes dispassionate and freed from defilements by not grasping.

segs.p: Rūpadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cittaṁ virattaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti anupādāya āsavehi, vedanādhātuyā …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant’s mind is dispassionate toward the form element, the feeling element,
the perception element,
the choices element,

segs.p: viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cittaṁ virattaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti anupādāya āsavehi.
segs.e: and the consciousness element, it’s freed from defilements by not grasping.

segs.p: Vimuttattā ṭhitaṁ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṁ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
Linked Discourses 22.46
5. Be Your Own Island
Impermanence (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, form is impermanent.
What’s impermanent is suffering.
What’s suffering is not-self.

segs.p: yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
Feeling is impermanent …
Perception is impermanent …
Choices are impermanent …
Consciousness is impermanent.
What’s impermanent is suffering.
What’s suffering is not-self.

segs.p: yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato pubbantānudiṭṭhiyo na honti.
segs.e: Seeing truly with right understanding like this, they have no theories about the first beginning.
Not having theories about the first beginning, they have no theories about the final end.

segs.p: Aparantānudiṭṭhīnaṁ asati, thāmaso parāmāso na hoti.
segs.e: Not having theories about the final end, they don’t obstinately stick to them.
Not misapprehending, the mind becomes dispassionate toward form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,

segs.p: viññāṇasmiṁ cittaṁ virajjati vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi.
segs.e: and consciousness; it’s freed from defilements by not grasping.

segs.p: Vimuttattā ṭhitaṁ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṁ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
Linked Discourses 22.47
5. Be Your Own Island
Ways of Regarding
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṁ attānaṁ samanupassamānā samanupassanti, sabbete pañcupādānakkhandhe samanupassanti, etesaṁ vā aññataraṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, whatever ascetics and brahmins regard various kinds of things as self, all regard the five grasping aggregates, or one of them.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto
segs.e: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
They regard feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Iti ayañceva samanupassanā ‘asmī’ti cassa avigataṁ hoti.
segs.e: So they’re not rid of this way of regarding things, and the conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: ‘Asmī’ti kho pana, bhikkhave, avigate pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ avakkanti hoti—
segs.e: As long as they’re not rid of the conceit ‘I am’, the five faculties are conceived—
the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, mano, atthi dhammā, atthi avijjādhātu.
segs.e: The mind, ideas, and the element of ignorance are all present.

segs.p: Avijjāsamphassajena, bhikkhave, vedayitena phuṭṭhassa assutavato puthujjanassa ‘asmī’tipissa hoti;
segs.e: Struck by feelings born of contact with ignorance, an unlearned ordinary person thinks ‘I am’,
‘I am this’,
‘I will be’,
‘I will not be’,
‘I will have form’,
‘I will be formless’,
‘I will be percipient’,
‘I will not be percipient’,
‘I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’.
The five faculties stay right where they are.

segs.p: Athettha sutavato ariyasāvakassa avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati.
segs.e: But a learned noble disciple gives up ignorance about them and gives rise to knowledge.
With the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge, they don’t think ‘I am’,
‘I am this’,
‘I will be’,
‘I will not be’,
‘I will have form’,
‘I will be formless’,
‘I will be percipient’,
‘I will be non-percipient’,
‘I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’.”
Linked Discourses 22.48
5. Be Your Own Island
Aggregates
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you the five aggregates and the five grasping aggregates.
Listen …
And what are the five aggregates?

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, ayaṁ vuccati rūpakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: this is called the aggregate of form.
Any kind of feeling at all …
Any kind of perception at all …

segs.p: ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā …pe… ayaṁ vuccati saṅkhārakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of choices at all …

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, ayaṁ vuccati viññāṇakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: this is called the aggregate of consciousness.
These are called the five aggregates.
And what are the five grasping aggregates?

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ …pe… yaṁ dūre santike vā sāsavaṁ upādāniyaṁ, ayaṁ vuccati rūpupādānakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near, which is accompanied by defilements and fuels grasping: this is called the grasping aggregate of form.

segs.p: Yā kāci vedanā …pe… yā dūre santike vā sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṁ vuccati vedanupādānakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of feeling at all …

segs.p: Yā kāci saññā …pe… yā dūre santike vā sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṁ vuccati saññupādānakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of perception at all …

segs.p: Ye keci saṅkhārā …pe… sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṁ vuccati saṅkhārupādānakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of choices at all …

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ …pe… yaṁ dūre santike vā sāsavaṁ upādāniyaṁ, ayaṁ vuccati viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
segs.e: Any kind of consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near, which is accompanied by defilements and fuels grasping: this is called the grasping aggregate of consciousness.
These are called the five grasping aggregates.”

5. Be Your Own Island
With Soṇa
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho soṇo gahapatiputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe…
segs.e: Then the householder Soṇa went up to the Buddha …

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho soṇaṁ gahapatiputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Ye hi keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā aniccena rūpena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti;
segs.e: “Soṇa, there are ascetics and brahmins who—based on form, which is impermanent, suffering, and perishable—regard themselves thus: ‘I’m better’,
or ‘I’m equal’,
or ‘I’m worse’.
What is that but a failure to see truly?

segs.p: Aniccāya vedanāya dukkhāya vipariṇāmadhammāya ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti;
segs.e: Based on feeling …
perception …

segs.p: aniccehi saṅkhārehi dukkhehi vipariṇāmadhammehi ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti;
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Aniccena viññāṇena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti;
segs.e: consciousness, which is impermanent, suffering, and perishable, they regard themselves thus: ‘I’m better’,
or ‘I’m equal’,
or ‘I’m worse’.
What is that but a failure to see truly?

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā aniccena rūpena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti;
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who—based on form, which is impermanent, suffering, and perishable—don’t regard themselves thus: ‘I’m better’,
or ‘I’m equal’,
or ‘I’m worse’.
What is that but seeing truly?
Based on feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: aniccena viññāṇena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti;
segs.e: consciousness, which is impermanent, suffering, and perishable, they don’t regard themselves thus: ‘I’m better’,
or ‘I’m equal’,
or ‘I’m worse’.
What is that but seeing truly?
What do you think, Soṇa?
Is form permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Tasmātiha, soṇa, yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: “So, Soṇa, you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
You should truly see any kind of feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, soṇa, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

5. Be Your Own Island
With Soṇa (2nd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho soṇo gahapatiputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho soṇaṁ gahapatiputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Soṇa went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Ye hi keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā rūpaṁ nappajānanti, rūpasamudayaṁ nappajānanti, rūpanirodhaṁ nappajānanti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānanti;
segs.e: “Soṇa, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

segs.p: vedanaṁ nappajānanti, vedanāsamudayaṁ nappajānanti, vedanānirodhaṁ nappajānanti, vedanānirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānanti;
segs.e: They don’t understand feeling …
perception …

segs.p: saṅkhāre nappajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānanti;
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ nappajānanti, viññāṇasamudayaṁ nappajānanti, viññāṇanirodhaṁ nappajānanti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānanti.
segs.e: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

segs.p: Na me te, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṁ vā brahmaññatthaṁ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.
segs.e: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā rūpaṁ pajānanti, rūpasamudayaṁ pajānanti, rūpanirodhaṁ pajānanti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti;
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
They do understand feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ pajānanti, viññāṇasamudayaṁ pajānanti, viññāṇanirodhaṁ pajānanti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti.
segs.e: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

segs.p: Te ca kho me, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.
segs.e: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”
Linked Discourses 22.51
5. Be Your Own Island
The End of Relishing
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Aniccaññeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaṁ aniccanti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, form really is impermanent. A mendicant sees that it is impermanent: that’s their right view.
Seeing rightly, they grow disillusioned.
When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.
When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.

segs.p: Aniccaññeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedanaṁ aniccanti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: Feeling …

segs.p: Aniccaññeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saññaṁ aniccanti passati …pe…
segs.e: Perception …

segs.p: anicceyeva bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅkhāre aniccāti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: Choices …

segs.p: Aniccaññeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu viññāṇaṁ aniccanti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: Consciousness really is impermanent. A mendicant sees that it is impermanent: that’s their right view.
Seeing rightly, they grow disillusioned.
When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.
When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.”
Linked Discourses 22.52
5. Be Your Own Island
The End of Relishing (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, rūpāniccatañca yathābhūtaṁ samanupassatha.
segs.e: “Mendicants, rationally apply the mind to form. Truly see the impermanence of form.

segs.p: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yoniso manasi karonto, rūpāniccatañca yathābhūtaṁ samanupassanto rūpasmiṁ nibbindati.
segs.e: When a mendicant does this, they grow disillusioned with form.
When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.
When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.

segs.p: Vedanaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, vedanāniccatañca yathābhūtaṁ samanupassatha.
segs.e: Rationally apply the mind to feeling …

segs.p: Vedanaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yoniso manasi karonto, vedanāniccatañca yathābhūtaṁ samanupassanto vedanāya nibbindati.

segs.e: perception …

segs.p: saṅkhāre, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, saṅkhārāniccatañca yathābhūtaṁ samanupassatha.
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Saṅkhāre, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yoniso manasi karonto, saṅkhārāniccataṁ yathābhūtaṁ samanupassanto saṅkhāresu nibbindati.
Viññāṇaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, viññāṇāniccatañca yathābhūtaṁ samanupassatha.
segs.e: consciousness. Truly see the impermanence of consciousness.

segs.p: Viññāṇaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yoniso manasi karonto, viññāṇāniccatañca yathābhūtaṁ samanupassanto viññāṇasmiṁ nibbindati.
segs.e: When a mendicant does this, they grow disillusioned with consciousness.
When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.
When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.”

6. Involvement
Involvement
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, if you get involved, you’re not free. If you’re not involved, you’re free.

segs.p: Rūpupayaṁ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya, rūpārammaṇaṁ rūpappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyya.
segs.e: Should consciousness involved with form, supported by form, established on form continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.
Or should consciousness involved with feeling remain …
Or should consciousness involved with perception remain …

segs.p: saṅkhārupayaṁ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya, saṅkhārārammaṇaṁ saṅkhārappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyya.
segs.e: Or should consciousness involved with choices, supported by choices, established on choices continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.
Mendicants, suppose you say:

segs.p: ‘ahamaññatra rūpā aññatra vedanāya aññatra saññāya aññatra saṅkhārehi viññāṇassa āgatiṁ vā gatiṁ vā cutiṁ vā upapattiṁ vā vuddhiṁ vā virūḷhiṁ vā vepullaṁ vā paññāpessāmī’ti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: ‘Apart from form, feeling, perception, and choices, I will describe the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and reappearing, its growth, increase, and maturity.’ That is not possible.

segs.p: Rūpadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti.
segs.e: If a mendicant has given up greed for the form element,

segs.p: Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṁ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.
If a mendicant has given up greed for the feeling element …
perception element …
choices element …

segs.p: viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti.
segs.e: consciousness element,

segs.p: Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṁ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.
Since that consciousness does not become established and does not grow, not making choices, it is freed.

segs.p: Vimuttattā ṭhitaṁ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṁ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

6. Involvement
Seeds of Plants
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, there are five kinds of plants.
What five?

segs.p: Mūlabījaṁ, khandhabījaṁ, aggabījaṁ, phalubījaṁ, bījabījaññeva pañcamaṁ.
segs.e: Plants propagated from roots, trunks, cuttings, or joints; and those from regular seeds are the fifth.

segs.p: Imāni cassu, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni akhaṇḍāni apūtikāni avātātapahatāni sārādāni sukhasayitāni, pathavī ca nāssa, āpo ca nāssa;
segs.e: Suppose these five kinds of plants were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. But there’s no earth or water.

segs.p: api numāni, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyyun”ti?
segs.e: Then would these five kinds of plants reach growth, increase, and maturity?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Imāni cassu, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni akhaṇḍāni …pe… sukhasayitāni, pathavī ca assa, āpo ca assa;
segs.e: “Suppose these five kinds of plants were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. And there is earth and water.

segs.p: api numāni, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyyun”ti?
segs.e: Then would these five kinds of plants reach growth, increase, and maturity?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātu, evaṁ catasso viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo daṭṭhabbā.
segs.e: “The four establishings of consciousness should be seen as like the earth element.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āpodhātu, evaṁ nandirāgo daṭṭhabbo.
segs.e: Relishing and greed should be seen as like the water element.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni, evaṁ viññāṇaṁ sāhāraṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: Consciousness with its fuel should be seen as like the five kinds of plants.

segs.p: Rūpupayaṁ, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya, rūpārammaṇaṁ rūpappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyya.
segs.e: Should consciousness involved with form, supported by form, established on form continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.

segs.p: Vedanupayaṁ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya …pe…
segs.e: Or should consciousness involved with feeling remain …

segs.p: saññupayaṁ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya …pe…
segs.e: Or should consciousness involved with perception remain …

segs.p: saṅkhārupayaṁ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya, saṅkhārārammaṇaṁ saṅkhārappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyya.
segs.e: Or should consciousness involved with choices, supported by choices, established on choices continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.
Mendicants, suppose you say:

segs.p: ‘ahamaññatra rūpā aññatra vedanāya aññatra saññāya aññatra saṅkhārehi viññāṇassa āgatiṁ vā gatiṁ vā cutiṁ vā upapattiṁ vā vuddhiṁ vā virūḷhiṁ vā vepullaṁ vā paññāpessāmī’ti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: ‘Apart from form, feeling, perception, and choices, I will describe the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and reappearing, its growth, increase, and maturity.’ That is not possible.

segs.p: Rūpadhātuyā ceva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti.
segs.e: If a mendicant has given up greed for the form element,

segs.p: Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṁ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.
If a mendicant has given up greed for the feeling element …
perception element …
choices element …

segs.p: viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti.
segs.e: consciousness element,

segs.p: Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṁ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.
Since that consciousness does not become established and does not grow, not making choices, it is freed.

segs.p: Vimuttattā ṭhitaṁ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṁ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.
They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended … there is nothing further for this place.’”

6. Involvement
An Inspired Saying
At Sāvatthī.
There the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:

segs.p: “‘no cassaṁ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti—
segs.e: “‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine.’

segs.p: evaṁ adhimuccamāno bhikkhu chindeyya orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanānī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who makes such a resolution can cut off the lower fetters.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “yathā kathaṁ pana, bhante, ‘no cassaṁ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti—
segs.e: “But sir, how

segs.p: evaṁ adhimuccamāno bhikkhu chindeyya orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanānī”ti?
segs.e: can a mendicant who makes such a resolution cut off the lower fetters?”

“Mendicant, take an unlearned ordinary person who has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in their teaching. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in their teaching.

segs.p: sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
They regard feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: So aniccaṁ rūpaṁ ‘aniccaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti,
segs.e: They don’t truly understand form—which is impermanent—as impermanent.
They don’t truly understand feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness—which is impermanent—as impermanent.
They don’t truly understand form—which is suffering—as suffering.
They don’t truly understand feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness—which is suffering—as suffering.
They don’t truly understand form—which is not-self—as not-self.
They don’t truly understand feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness—which is not-self—as not-self.
They don’t truly understand form—which is conditioned—as conditioned.
They don’t truly understand feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness—which is conditioned—as conditioned.
They don’t truly understand that form will vanish.
They don’t truly understand that feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness will vanish.

segs.p: Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhu, ariyasāvako ariyānaṁ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṁ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto
segs.e: But a learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.
They don’t regard form as self …
They don’t regard feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness as self.

segs.p: So aniccaṁ rūpaṁ ‘aniccaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: They truly understand form—which is impermanent—as impermanent.
They truly understand feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness—which is impermanent—as impermanent.
They truly understand form … feeling … perception … choices … consciousness—which is suffering—as suffering.
They truly understand form … feeling … perception … choices … consciousness—which is not-self—as not-self.

segs.p: saṅkhataṁ rūpaṁ …pe… saṅkhataṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘saṅkhataṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: They truly understand form … feeling … perception … choices … consciousness—which is conditioned—as conditioned.
They truly understand that form will vanish.
They truly understand that feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness will vanish.

segs.p: So rūpassa vibhavā, vedanāya vibhavā, saññāya vibhavā, saṅkhārānaṁ vibhavā, viññāṇassa vibhavā, evaṁ kho, bhikkhu,
segs.e: It’s because of the vanishing of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness that a mendicant who makes such a resolution—

segs.p: ‘no cassaṁ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti—
segs.e: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine’—

segs.p: evaṁ adhimuccamāno bhikkhu chindeyya orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanānī”ti.
segs.e: can cut off the lower fetters.”
“Sir, you say that a mendicant who makes such a resolution can cut off the lower fetters.

segs.p: Kathaṁ pana, bhante, jānato kathaṁ passato anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hotī”ti?
segs.e: But how are they to know and see in order to end the defilements without delay?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, assutavā puthujjano atasitāye ṭhāne tāsaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: “Mendicant, an unlearned ordinary person worries about things that aren’t a worry.
For an unlearned ordinary person worries:

segs.p: ‘no cassaṁ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine.’

segs.p: Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhu, ariyasāvako atasitāye ṭhāne na tāsaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: A learned noble disciple doesn’t worry about things that aren’t a worry.

segs.p: Na heso, bhikkhu, tāso sutavato ariyasāvakassa:
segs.e: For a learned noble disciple doesn’t worry:

segs.p: ‘no cassaṁ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine.’

segs.p: Rūpupayaṁ vā, bhikkhu, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya, rūpārammaṇaṁ rūpappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyya.
segs.e: Should consciousness involved with form, supported by form, established on form continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.
Or should consciousness involved with feeling remain …
Or should consciousness involved with perception remain …

segs.p: saṅkhārupayaṁ vā, bhikkhu, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭheyya, saṅkhārārammaṇaṁ saṅkhārappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyya.
segs.e: Or should consciousness involved with choices, supported by choices, established on choices continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.
Suppose, mendicant, you were to say:

segs.p: ‘ahamaññatra rūpā, aññatra vedanāya, aññatra saññāya, aññatra saṅkhārehi viññāṇassa āgatiṁ vā gatiṁ vā cutiṁ vā upapattiṁ vā vuddhiṁ vā virūḷhiṁ vā vepullaṁ vā paññāpessāmī’ti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: ‘Apart from form, feeling, perception, and choices, I will describe the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and reappearing, its growth, increase, and maturity.’ That is not possible.

segs.p: Rūpadhātuyā ce, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṁ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: If a mendicant has given up greed for the form element, the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.
If a mendicant has given up greed for the feeling element …
perception element …
choices element …

segs.p: viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṁ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: consciousness element, the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.
Since that consciousness does not become established and does not grow, not making choices, it is freed.

segs.p: Vimuttattā ṭhitaṁ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṁ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.
They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended … there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, jānato evaṁ passato anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hotī”ti.
segs.e: The ending of the defilements without delay is for one who knows and sees this.”
Linked Discourses 22.56
6. Involvement
Rounds of the Grasping Aggregates
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, there are these five grasping aggregates.
What five?
The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ime pañcupādānakkhandhe catuparivaṭṭaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññāsiṁ, neva tāvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṁ.
segs.e: As long as I didn’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates in four rounds, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

segs.p: Yato ca khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ime pañcupādānakkhandhe catuparivaṭṭaṁ yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, athāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke …pe…
segs.e: But when I did truly understand these five grasping aggregates in four rounds, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.
And how are there four rounds?

segs.p: Rūpaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, rūpasamudayaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, rūpanirodhaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ;
segs.e: I directly knew form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
I directly knew feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, viññāṇasamudayaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, viññāṇanirodhaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ.
segs.e: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
And what is form?

segs.p: Cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṁ upādāya rūpaṁ.
segs.e: The four principal states, and form derived from the four principal states.
This is called form.
Form originates from fuel.
When fuel ceases, form ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo rūpanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of form is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ rūpaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpanirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya rūpassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā.
segs.e: Whatever ascetics and brahmins have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form: they are practicing well.

segs.p: Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti.
segs.e: Those who practice well have a footing in this teaching and training.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ rūpaṁ abhiññāya …pe… evaṁ rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya, rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā te suvimuttā.
segs.e: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.
Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

segs.p: Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṁ tesaṁ natthi paññāpanāya.
segs.e: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.
And what is feeling?
There are these six classes of feeling:

segs.p: cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā.
segs.e: feeling born of contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
This is called feeling.
Feeling originates from contact.
When contact ceases, feeling ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of feelings is simply this noble eightfold path …

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ vedanaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanāsamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanānirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanānirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya vedanāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā.
Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti.
Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ vedanaṁ abhiññāya …pe… evaṁ vedanānirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya …pe…

segs.e: And what is perception?
There are these six classes of perception:

segs.p: rūpasaññā, saddasaññā, gandhasaññā, rasasaññā, phoṭṭhabbasaññā, dhammasaññā.
segs.e: perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.
This is called perception.
Perception originates from contact.
When contact ceases, perception ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of perceptions is simply this noble eightfold path …
And what are choices?
There are these six classes of intention:

segs.p: rūpasañcetanā, saddasañcetanā, gandhasañcetanā, rasasañcetanā, phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā, dhammasañcetanā.
segs.e: intention regarding sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.
These are called choices.
Choices originate from contact.
When contact ceases, choices cease.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅkhāranirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of choices is simply this noble eightfold path …

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ saṅkhāre abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhārasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhāranirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya saṅkhārānaṁ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā.
Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ saṅkhāre abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhārasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhāranirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya saṅkhārānaṁ nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā.
Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṁ tesaṁ natthi paññāpanāya.

segs.e: And what is consciousness?
There are these six classes of consciousness:

segs.p: cakkhuviññāṇaṁ, sotaviññāṇaṁ, ghānaviññāṇaṁ, jivhāviññāṇaṁ, kāyaviññāṇaṁ, manoviññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.
This is called consciousness.
Consciousness originates from name and form.
When name and form cease, consciousness ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viññāṇanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of consciousness is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ viññāṇaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā.
segs.e: Whatever ascetics and brahmins have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness: they are practicing well.

segs.p: Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti.
segs.e: Those who practice well have a footing in this teaching and training.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ viññāṇaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā.
segs.e: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.
Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

segs.p: Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṁ tesaṁ natthi paññāpanāyā”ti.
segs.e: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.”
Linked Discourses 22.57
6. Involvement
Seven Cases
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Sattaṭṭhānakusalo, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tividhūpaparikkhī imasmiṁ dhammavinaye kevalī vusitavā uttamapurisoti vuccati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in this teaching and training a mendicant who is skilled in seven cases and who examines in three ways is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.
And how is a mendicant skilled in seven cases?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaṁ pajānāti, rūpasamudayaṁ pajānāti, rūpanirodhaṁ pajānāti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant understands form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

segs.p: rūpassa assādaṁ pajānāti, rūpassa ādīnavaṁ pajānāti, rūpassa nissaraṇaṁ pajānāti;
segs.e: They understand form’s gratification, drawback, and escape.
They understand feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇasamudayaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti;
segs.e: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

segs.p: viññāṇassa assādaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇassa ādīnavaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand consciousness’s gratification, drawback, and escape.
And what is form?

segs.p: Cattāro ca mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṁ upādāya rūpaṁ.
segs.e: The four principal states, and form derived from the four principal states.
This is called form.
Form originates from fuel.
When fuel ceases, form ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo rūpanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of form is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yaṁ rūpaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ—
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness that arise from form: this is its gratification.
That form is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.
Removing and giving up desire and greed for form: this is its escape.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ rūpaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpanirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya;
segs.e: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

segs.p: evaṁ rūpassa assādaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpassa ādīnavaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpassa nissaraṇaṁ abhiññāya rūpassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā.
segs.e: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form: they are practicing well.

segs.p: Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti.
segs.e: Those who practice well have a footing in this teaching and training.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ rūpaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpanirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya;
segs.e: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

segs.p: evaṁ rūpassa assādaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpassa ādīnavaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ rūpassa nissaraṇaṁ abhiññāya rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā.
segs.e: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.
Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

segs.p: Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṁ tesaṁ natthi paññāpanāya.
segs.e: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.
And what is feeling?
There are these six classes of feeling:
feeling born of eye contact …
feeling born of mind contact.
This is called feeling.
Feeling originates from contact.
When contact ceases, feeling ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of feelings is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yaṁ vedanaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ—
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness that arise from feeling: this is its gratification.
That feeling is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.
Removing and giving up desire and greed for feeling: this is its escape. …

segs.p: Ye hi, keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ vedanaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanāsamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanānirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanānirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya;
evaṁ vedanāya assādaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanāya ādīnavaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ vedanāya nissaraṇaṁ abhiññāya vedanāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā.
Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti.
Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ vedanaṁ abhiññāya …pe…

segs.e: And what is perception?
There are these six classes of perception:

segs.p: rūpasaññā, saddasaññā, gandhasaññā, rasasaññā, phoṭṭhabbasaññā, dhammasaññā.
segs.e: perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.
This is called perception.
Perception originates from contact.
When contact ceases, perception ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of perceptions is simply this noble eightfold path …
And what are choices?
There are these six classes of intention:
intention regarding sights …
intention regarding ideas.
These are called choices.
Choices originate from contact.
When contact ceases, choices cease.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅkhāranirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of choices is simply this noble eightfold path …

segs.p: Yaṁ saṅkhāre paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ—

Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ saṅkhāre abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhārasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhāranirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya …pe… saṅkhārānaṁ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā te suppaṭipannā.
Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti …pe…

segs.e: And what is consciousness?
There are these six classes of consciousness:

segs.p: cakkhuviññāṇaṁ, sotaviññāṇaṁ, ghānaviññāṇaṁ, jivhāviññāṇaṁ, kāyaviññāṇaṁ, manoviññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.
This is called consciousness.
Consciousness originates from name and form.
When name and form cease, consciousness ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viññāṇanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of consciousness is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yaṁ viññāṇaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ—
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness that arise from consciousness: this is its gratification.
That consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.
Removing and giving up desire and greed for consciousness: this is its escape.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ viññāṇaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya;
segs.e: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

segs.p: evaṁ viññāṇassa assādaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇassa ādīnavaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṁ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā.
segs.e: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness: they are practicing well.

segs.p: Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye gādhanti.
segs.e: Those who practice well have a footing  in this teaching and training.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṁ viññāṇaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇasamudayaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ abhiññāya;
segs.e: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

segs.p: evaṁ viññāṇassa assādaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇassa ādīnavaṁ abhiññāya, evaṁ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṁ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā.
segs.e: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.
Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

segs.p: Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṁ tesaṁ natthi paññāpanāya.
segs.e: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattaṭṭhānakusalo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is skilled in seven cases.
And how does a mendicant examine in three ways?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhātuso upaparikkhati, āyatanaso upaparikkhati, paṭiccasamuppādaso upaparikkhati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant examines by way of the elements, sense fields, and dependent origination.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tividhūpaparikkhī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant examines in three ways.

segs.p: Sattaṭṭhānakusalo, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tividhūpaparikkhī, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye kevalī vusitavā ‘uttamapuriso’ti vuccatī”ti.
segs.e: In this teaching and training, a mendicant who is skilled in seven cases and who examines in three ways is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.”
Linked Discourses 22.58
6. Involvement
The Fully Awakened Buddha
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Tathāgato, bhikkhave, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto sammāsambuddhoti vuccati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha is freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form. They’re called a fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Bhikkhupi, bhikkhave, paññāvimutto rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto paññāvimuttoti vuccati.
segs.e: A mendicant freed by wisdom is also freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form. They’re called a mendicant freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Tathāgato, bhikkhave, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vedanāya nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto sammāsambuddhoti vuccati.
segs.e: A Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha is freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding feeling …

segs.p: Bhikkhupi, bhikkhave, paññāvimutto vedanāya nibbidā …pe… paññāvimuttoti vuccati.

segs.e: perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto sammāsambuddhoti vuccati.
segs.e: consciousness. They’re called a fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Bhikkhupi, bhikkhave, paññāvimutto viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto paññāvimuttoti vuccati.
segs.e: A mendicant freed by wisdom is also freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness. They’re called a mendicant freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Tatra kho, bhikkhave, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso, kiṁ nānākaraṇaṁ, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa paññāvimuttena bhikkhunā”ti?
segs.e: What, then, is the difference between a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, and a mendicant freed by wisdom?”

segs.p: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṁnettikā bhagavaṁpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaññeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Tathāgato, bhikkhave, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā, asañjātassa maggassa sañjanetā, anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā maggaññū, maggavidū, maggakovido;
segs.e: “The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha gave rise to the unarisen path, gave birth to the unborn path, and explained the unexplained path. He is the knower of the path, the discoverer of the path, the expert on the path.

segs.p: maggānugā ca, bhikkhave, etarahi sāvakā viharanti pacchā samannāgatā.
segs.e: And now the disciples live following the path; they acquire it later.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso, ayaṁ adhippayāso, idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa paññāvimuttena bhikkhunā”ti.
segs.e: This is the difference between a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, and a mendicant freed by wisdom.”
Linked Discourses 22.59
6. Involvement
The Characteristic of Not-Self

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha addressed the group of five mendicants:
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, form is not-self.

segs.p: Rūpañca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṁ rūpaṁ ābādhāya saṁvatteyya, labbhetha ca rūpe:
segs.e: For if form were self, it wouldn’t lead to affliction. And you could compel form:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ me rūpaṁ hotu, evaṁ me rūpaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
segs.e: ‘May my form be like this! May it not be like that!’

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ anattā, tasmā rūpaṁ ābādhāya saṁvattati, na ca labbhati rūpe:
segs.e: But because form is not-self, it leads to affliction. And you can’t compel form:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ me rūpaṁ hotu, evaṁ me rūpaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
segs.e: ‘May my form be like this! May it not be like that!’
Feeling is not-self …

segs.p: Vedanā ca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṁ vedanā ābādhāya saṁvatteyya, labbhetha ca vedanāya:
‘evaṁ me vedanā hotu, evaṁ me vedanā mā ahosī’ti.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, vedanā anattā, tasmā vedanā ābādhāya saṁvattati, na ca labbhati vedanāya:
‘evaṁ me vedanā hotu, evaṁ me vedanā mā ahosī’ti.

segs.e: Perception is not-self …
Choices are not-self …

segs.p: Saṅkhārā ca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissaṁsu, nayidaṁ saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṁvatteyyuṁ, labbhetha ca saṅkhāresu:
‘evaṁ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṁ me saṅkhārā mā ahesun’ti.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā anattā, tasmā saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṁvattanti, na ca labbhati saṅkhāresu:
‘evaṁ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṁ me saṅkhārā mā ahesun’ti.

segs.e: Consciousness is not-self.

segs.p: Viññāṇañca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṁ viññāṇaṁ ābādhāya saṁvatteyya, labbhetha ca viññāṇe:
segs.e: For if consciousness were self, it wouldn’t lead to affliction. And you could compel consciousness:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ hotu, evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
segs.e: ‘May my consciousness be like this! May it not be like that!’

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ anattā, tasmā viññāṇaṁ ābādhāya saṁvattati, na ca labbhati viññāṇe:
segs.e: But because consciousness is not-self, it leads to affliction. And you can’t compel consciousness:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ hotu, evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
segs.e: ‘May my consciousness be like this! May it not be like that!’
What do you think, mendicants?
Is form permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is feeling permanent or impermanent?” …
“Is perception permanent or impermanent?” …
“Are choices permanent or impermanent?” …
“Is consciousness permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: “So you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā …pe… yā dūre santike vā, sabbā vedanā: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: Any kind of feeling at all …
Any kind of perception at all …

segs.p: ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā …pe… ye dūre santike vā, sabbe saṅkhārā: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: Any kind of choices at all …

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should truly see any kind of consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanduṁ.
segs.e: Satisfied, the group of five mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne pañcavaggiyānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṁsūti.
segs.e: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the group of five mendicants were freed from defilements by not grasping.
Linked Discourses 22.60
6. Involvement
With Mahāli
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho mahāli licchavi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mahāli licchavi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahāli the Licchavi went up to the Buddha … and said to him:
“Sir, Pūraṇa Kassapa says this:
‘There is no cause or reason for the corruption of sentient beings.
Sentient beings are corrupted without cause or reason.

segs.p: Natthi hetu natthi paccayo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā;
segs.e: There’s no cause or reason for the purification of sentient beings.
Sentient beings are purified without cause or reason.’
What does the Buddha say about this?”

segs.p: “Atthi, mahāli, hetu atthi paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya;
segs.e: “Mahāli, there is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings.
Sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason.

segs.p: Atthi, mahāli, hetu, atthi paccayo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā;
segs.e: There is a cause and reason for the purification of sentient beings.
Sentient beings are purified with cause and reason.”

segs.p: “Katamo pana, bhante, hetu katamo paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya;
segs.e: “But sir, what is the cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings?
How are sentient beings corrupted with cause and reason?”

segs.p: “Rūpañca hidaṁ, mahāli, ekantadukkhaṁ abhavissa dukkhānupatitaṁ dukkhāvakkantaṁ anavakkantaṁ sukhena, nayidaṁ sattā rūpasmiṁ sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: “Mahāli, if form were absolutely painful—soaked and steeped in pain and not steeped in pleasure—sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, rūpaṁ sukhaṁ sukhānupatitaṁ sukhāvakkantaṁ anavakkantaṁ dukkhena, tasmā sattā rūpasmiṁ sārajjanti;
segs.e: But because form is pleasurable—soaked and steeped in pleasure and not steeped in pain—sentient beings are aroused by it.
Since they are aroused by it, they’re caught up in it, and so they become corrupted.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya;
segs.e: This is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings.
This is how sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason.

segs.p: Vedanā ca hidaṁ, mahāli, ekantadukkhā abhavissa dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, nayidaṁ sattā vedanāya sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If feeling …

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, vedanā sukhā sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā anavakkantā dukkhena, tasmā sattā vedanāya sārajjanti;
Ayampi kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya.

segs.e: perception …

segs.p: saṅkhārā ca hidaṁ, mahāli, ekantadukkhā abhavissaṁsu dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, nayidaṁ sattā saṅkhāresu sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, saṅkhārā sukhā sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā anavakkantā dukkhena, tasmā sattā saṅkhāresu sārajjanti;
Ayampi kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya.
Viññāṇañca hidaṁ, mahāli, ekantadukkhaṁ abhavissa dukkhānupatitaṁ dukkhāvakkantaṁ anavakkantaṁ sukhena, nayidaṁ sattā viññāṇasmiṁ sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: consciousness were absolutely painful—soaked and steeped in pain and not steeped in pleasure—sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, viññāṇaṁ sukhaṁ sukhānupatitaṁ sukhāvakkantaṁ anavakkantaṁ dukkhena, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmiṁ sārajjanti;
segs.e: But because consciousness is pleasurable—soaked and steeped in pleasure and not steeped in pain—sentient beings are aroused by it.
Since they are aroused by it, they’re caught up in it, and so they become corrupted.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, mahāli, hetu ayaṁ paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya.
segs.e: This is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings.
This is how sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason.”

segs.p: “Katamo pana, bhante, hetu katamo paccayo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā;
segs.e: “But sir, what is the cause and reason for the purification of sentient beings?
How are sentient beings purified with cause and reason?”

segs.p: “Rūpañca hidaṁ, mahāli, ekantasukhaṁ abhavissa sukhānupatitaṁ sukhāvakkantaṁ anavakkantaṁ dukkhena, nayidaṁ sattā rūpasmiṁ nibbindeyyuṁ.
segs.e: “Mahāli, if form was absolutely pleasurable—soaked and steeped in pleasure and not steeped in pain—sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

segs.e: But because form is painful—soaked and steeped in pain and not steeped in pleasure—sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.
Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they are purified.

6. Involvement
Burning
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, ādittaṁ, vedanā ādittā, saññā ādittā, saṅkhārā ādittā, viññāṇaṁ ādittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are burning.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi … saññāyapi … saṅkhāresupi … viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, niruttipathā adhivacanapathā paññattipathā asaṅkiṇṇā asaṅkiṇṇapubbā, na saṅkīyanti, na saṅkīyissanti, appaṭikuṭṭhā samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three scopes of definition, labeling, and description. They’re uncorrupted, as they have been since the beginning. They’re not being corrupted now, nor will they be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on them.

segs.e: choices …
