A Lump of Cow Dung
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “atthi nu kho, bhante, kiñci rūpaṁ yaṁ rūpaṁ niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassati?
segs.e: “Sir, is there any form at all that’s permanent, everlasting, eternal, imperishable, and will last forever and ever?

segs.p: Atthi nu kho, bhante, kāci vedanā yā vedanā niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammā sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassati?
segs.e: Is there any feeling …

segs.p: Atthi nu kho, bhante, kāci saññā yā saññā …pe…
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: atthi nu kho, bhante, keci saṅkhārā ye saṅkhārā niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammā sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassanti?
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Atthi nu kho, bhante, kiñci viññāṇaṁ, yaṁ viññāṇaṁ niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassatī”ti?
segs.e: consciousness at all that’s permanent, everlasting, eternal, imperishable, and will last forever and ever?”

segs.p: “Natthi kho, bhikkhu, kiñci rūpaṁ, yaṁ rūpaṁ niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassati.
segs.e: “Mendicant, there is no form at all that’s permanent, everlasting, eternal, imperishable, and will last forever and ever.
There’s no feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: kiñci viññāṇaṁ, yaṁ viññāṇaṁ niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassatī”ti.
segs.e: consciousness at all that’s permanent, everlasting, eternal, imperishable, and will last forever and ever.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā parittaṁ gomayapiṇḍaṁ pāṇinā gahetvā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, picking up a lump of cow dung, said to the mendicant:

segs.p: “ettakopi kho, bhikkhu, attabhāvapaṭilābho natthi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassati.
segs.e: “There’s not even this much of any incarnation that’s permanent, everlasting, eternal, imperishable, and will last forever and ever.

segs.p: Ettako cepi, bhikkhu, attabhāvapaṭilābho abhavissa nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo, nayidaṁ brahmacariyavāso paññāyetha sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: If there were, this living of the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering would not be found.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhu, ettakopi attabhāvapaṭilābho natthi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo, tasmā brahmacariyavāso paññāyati sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: But since there isn’t, this living of the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering is found.

segs.p: Bhūtapubbāhaṁ, bhikkhu, rājā ahosiṁ khattiyo muddhāvasitto.
segs.e: Once upon a time I was an anointed aristocratic king.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītinagarasahassāni ahesuṁ kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 cities, with the capital Kusāvatī the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītipāsādasahassāni ahesuṁ dhammapāsādappamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 palaces, with the Palace of Principle the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītikūṭāgārasahassāni ahesuṁ mahābyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 chambers, with the Chamber of the Grand Tower the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītipallaṅkasahassāni ahesuṁ dantamayāni sāramayāni sovaṇṇamayāni goṇakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 couches made of ivory or heartwood or gold or silver, spread with woolen covers—shag-piled or embroidered with flowers—and spread with a fine deer hide, with a canopy above and red pillows at both ends.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītināgasahassāni ahesuṁ sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇaddhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 bull elephants with gold adornments and banners, covered with snow gold netting, with the royal bull elephant named Sabbath the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītiassasahassāni ahesuṁ sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇaddhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 horses with gold adornments and banners, covered with snow gold netting, with the royal steed named Thundercloud the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītirathasahassāni ahesuṁ sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇaddhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 chariots with gold adornments and banners, covered with snow gold netting, with the chariot named Triumph the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu, rañño sato khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa caturāsītimaṇisahassāni ahesuṁ maṇiratanappamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 jewels, with the jewel-treasure the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu …pe… caturāsītiitthisahassāni ahesuṁ subhaddādevippamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 women, with Queen Subhaddā the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu …pe… caturāsītikhattiyasahassāni ahesuṁ anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 aristocrat vassals, with the commander-treasure the foremost.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu …pe… caturāsītidhenusahassāni ahesuṁ dukūlasandānāni kaṁsūpadhāraṇāni.
segs.e: I had 84,000 milk cows with muslin halter and bronze pails.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu …pe… caturāsītivatthakoṭisahassāni ahesuṁ khomasukhumāni koseyyasukhumāni kambalasukhumāni kappāsikasukhumāni.
segs.e: I had 8,400,000,000 cloths of delicate linen, cotton, silk, and wool.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhu …pe… caturāsītithālipākasahassāni ahesuṁ; sāyaṁ pātaṁ bhattābhihāro abhihariyittha.
segs.e: I had 84,000 servings of food, which were presented to me as offerings at daybreak and dusk.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā nagarasahassānaṁ ekaññeva taṁ nagaraṁ hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi—kusāvatī rājadhānī.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 cities, I only stayed in one, the capital Kusāvatī.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā pāsādasahassānaṁ ekoyeva so pāsādo hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi—dhammo pāsādo.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 palaces, I only dwelt in one, the Palace of Principle.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā kūṭāgārasahassānaṁ ekaññeva taṁ kūṭāgāraṁ hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi—mahābyūhaṁ kūṭāgāraṁ.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 chambers, I only dwelt in one, the  Chamber of the Grand Tower.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā pallaṅkasahassānaṁ ekoyeva so pallaṅko hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena paribhuñjāmi—dantamayo vā sāramayo vā sovaṇṇamayo vā rūpiyamayo vā.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 couches, I only used one, made of ivory or heartwood or gold or silver.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā nāgasahassānaṁ ekoyeva so nāgo hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena abhiruhāmi—uposatho nāgarājā.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 bull elephants, I only rode one, the royal bull elephant named Sabbath.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā assasahassānaṁ ekoyeva so asso hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena abhiruhāmi—valāhako assarājā.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 horses, I only rode one, the royal horse named Thundercloud.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā rathasahassānaṁ ekoyeva so ratho hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena abhiruhāmi—vejayanto ratho.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 chariots, I only rode one, the chariot named Triumph.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā itthisahassānaṁ ekāyeva sā itthī hoti yā maṁ tena samayena paccupaṭṭhāti—khattiyānī vā velāmikā vā.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 women, I was only served by one, an aristocrat maiden or a coquette.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā vatthakoṭisahassānaṁ ekaññeva taṁ vatthayugaṁ hoti yamahaṁ tena samayena paridahāmi—khomasukhumaṁ vā koseyyasukhumaṁ vā kambalasukhumaṁ vā kappāsikasukhumaṁ vā.
segs.e: Of those 8,400,000,000 cloths, I only wore one pair, made of delicate linen, cotton, silk, and wool.

segs.p: Tesaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, caturāsītiyā thālipākasahassānaṁ ekoyeva so thālipāko hoti yato nāḷikodanaparamaṁ bhuñjāmi tadupiyañca sūpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: Of those 84,000 servings of food, I only had one, eating at most a cup of rice with suitable sauce.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhu, sabbe te saṅkhārā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā.
segs.e: And so all those conditioned phenomena have passed, ceased, and perished.
So impermanent are conditions,
so unstable are conditions,
so unreliable are conditions.

segs.p: Yāvañcidaṁ, bhikkhu, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṁ, alaṁ virajjituṁ, alaṁ vimuccitun”ti.
segs.e: This is quite enough for you to become disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed regarding all conditions.”

segs.e: Then the Buddha, picking up a little bit of dirt on his fingernail, said to that mendicant:

segs.p: “ettakampi kho, bhikkhu, rūpaṁ natthi niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassati.
segs.e: “There’s not even this much of any form that’s permanent, everlasting, eternal, imperishable, and will last forever and ever.

segs.p: Ettakañcepi, bhikkhu, rūpaṁ abhavissa niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ, nayidaṁ brahmacariyavāso paññāyetha sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: If there were, this living of the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering would not be found.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhu, ettakampi rūpaṁ natthi niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ, tasmā brahmacariyavāso paññāyati sammā dukkhakkhayāya”.
segs.e: But since there isn’t, this living of the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering is found.

segs.p: Ettakāpi kho, bhikkhu, vedanā natthi niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammā sassatisamaṁ tatheva ṭhassati.

“Mendicants, this transmigration has no known beginning.

segs.p: Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ sandhāvataṁ saṁsarataṁ.
segs.e: No first point is found of sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving.

segs.p: Hoti so, bhikkhave, samayo yaṁ mahāsamuddo ussussati visussati na bhavati;
segs.e: There comes a time when the ocean dries up and evaporates and is no more.

segs.p: na tvevāhaṁ, bhikkhave, avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ sandhāvataṁ saṁsarataṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering for sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving, I say.

segs.p: Hoti so, bhikkhave, samayo yaṁ sineru pabbatarājā ḍayhati vinassati na bhavati;
segs.e: There comes a time when Sineru the king of mountains is burned up and destroyed, and is no more.

segs.p: na tvevāhaṁ, bhikkhave, avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ sandhāvataṁ saṁsarataṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering for sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving, I say.

segs.p: Hoti so, bhikkhave, samayo yaṁ mahāpathavī ḍayhati vinassati na bhavati;
segs.e: There comes a time when the great earth is burned up and destroyed, and is no more.

segs.p: na tvevāhaṁ, bhikkhave, avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ sandhāvataṁ saṁsarataṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering for sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving, I say.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sā gaddulabaddho daḷhe khīle vā thambhe vā upanibaddho tameva khīlaṁ vā thambhaṁ vā anuparidhāvati anuparivattati;
segs.e: Suppose a hound on a leash was tethered to a strong post or pillar. It would just keep running and circling around that post or pillar.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī …pe…
segs.e: In the same way, take an unlearned ordinary person who has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in their teaching. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in their teaching.
They regard form …
feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: So rūpaññeva anuparidhāvati anuparivattati, vedanaññeva …pe… saññaññeva … saṅkhāreyeva … viññāṇaññeva anuparidhāvati anuparivattati.
segs.e: They just keep running and circling around form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: So rūpaṁ anuparidhāvaṁ anuparivattaṁ, vedanaṁ …pe… saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ anuparidhāvaṁ anuparivattaṁ, na parimuccati rūpamhā, na parimuccati vedanāya, na parimuccati saññāya, na parimuccati saṅkhārehi, na parimuccati viññāṇamhā, na parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
segs.e: Doing so, they’re not freed from form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. They’re not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
They’re not freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ariyānaṁ dassāvī …pe… sappurisadhamme suvinīto,
segs.e: A learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.
They don’t regard form …
feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā viññāṇaṁ, na viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: or consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: So rūpaṁ nānuparidhāvati nānuparivattati, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ nānuparidhāvati nānuparivattati.
segs.e: They don’t keep running and circling around form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: So rūpaṁ ananuparidhāvaṁ ananuparivattaṁ, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ ananuparidhāvaṁ ananuparivattaṁ; parimuccati rūpamhā, parimuccati vedanāya, parimuccati saññāya, parimuccati saṅkhārehi, parimuccati viññāṇamhā, parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
segs.e: By not doing so, they’re freed from form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
They’re freed from suffering, I say.”

segs.p: Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ sandhāvataṁ saṁsarataṁ.
segs.e: No first point is found of sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sā gaddulabaddho daḷhe khīle vā thambhe vā upanibaddho. So gacchati cepi tameva khīlaṁ vā thambhaṁ vā upagacchati; tiṭṭhati cepi tameva khīlaṁ vā thambhaṁ vā upatiṭṭhati; nisīdati cepi tameva khīlaṁ vā thambhaṁ vā upanisīdati; nipajjati cepi tameva khīlaṁ vā thambhaṁ vā upanipajjati.
segs.e: Suppose a mutt on a leash was tethered to a strong post or pillar. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, it stays right beside that post or pillar.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano rūpaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati.
segs.e: In the same way, an unlearned ordinary person regards form like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’
They regard feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati.
segs.e: consciousness like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

segs.p: So gacchati cepi ime pañcupādānakkhandhe upagacchati;
segs.e: When walking, they walk right beside the five grasping aggregates.
When standing …
sitting …
lying down, they lie down right beside the five grasping aggregates.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, abhikkhaṇaṁ sakaṁ cittaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should regularly check your own mind:
‘For a long time this mind has been corrupted by greed, hate, and delusion.’
Sentient beings are corrupted because the mind is corrupted.
Sentient beings are purified because the mind is purified.

segs.p: Diṭṭhaṁ vo, bhikkhave, caraṇaṁ nāma cittan”ti?
segs.e: Mendicants, have you seen the painting named ‘Conduct’?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Tampi kho, bhikkhave, caraṇaṁ nāma cittaṁ citteneva cittitaṁ. Tenapi kho, bhikkhave, caraṇena cittena cittaññeva cittataraṁ.
segs.e: “That painting was devised by the mind, but the mind is even more diverse than that.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, abhikkhaṇaṁ sakaṁ cittaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should regularly check your own mind:
‘For a long time this mind has been corrupted by greed, hate, and delusion.’
Sentient beings are corrupted because the mind is corrupted.
Sentient beings are purified because the mind is purified.

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekanikāyampi samanupassāmi evaṁ cittaṁ yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā.
segs.e: I don’t see any other order of beings as elaborate as the animal realm.

segs.p: tepi kho, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā citteneva cittitā, tehipi kho, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatehi pāṇehi cittaññeva cittataraṁ.
segs.e: The creatures in the animal realm were devised by the mind, but the mind is even more diverse than that.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, abhikkhaṇaṁ sakaṁ cittaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should regularly check your own mind:
‘For a long time this mind has been corrupted by greed, hate, and delusion.’
Sentient beings are corrupted because the mind is corrupted.
Sentient beings are purified because the mind is purified.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rajako vā cittakārako vā rajanāya vā lākhāya vā haliddiyā vā nīliyā vā mañjiṭṭhāya vā suparimaṭṭhe phalake vā bhittiyā vā dussapaṭṭe vā itthirūpaṁ vā purisarūpaṁ vā abhinimmineyya sabbaṅgapaccaṅgiṁ;
segs.e: Suppose an artist or painter had some dye, red lac, turmeric, indigo, or rose madder. And on a polished plank or a wall or a canvas they’d create the form of a woman or a man, whole in its major and minor limbs.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano rūpaññeva abhinibbattento abhinibbatteti, vedanaññeva …pe… saññaññeva … saṅkhāreyeva … viññāṇaññeva abhinibbattento abhinibbatteti.
segs.e: In the same way, when an unlearned ordinary person generates a future life, all they generate is form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
What do you think, mendicants?
Is form permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”
“Is feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness permanent or impermanent?” …
“So you should truly see …
Seeing this …
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

10. Flowers
The Adze
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Jānato ahaṁ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṁ khayaṁ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I say that the ending of defilements is for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know or see.

segs.p: Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiṁ passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti?
segs.e: For one who knows and sees what?

segs.p: ‘Iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
segs.e: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.
Such is feeling …
Such is perception …
Such are choices …

segs.p: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti—
segs.e: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

segs.p: evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṁ passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti.
segs.e: The ending of the defilements is for one who knows and sees this.

segs.p: Bhāvanānuyogaṁ ananuyuttassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno viharato kiñcāpi evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: When a mendicant is not committed to development, they might wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata me anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucceyyā’ti, atha khvassa neva anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: ‘If only my mind were freed from the defilements by not grasping!’ Even so, their mind is not freed from defilements by not grasping.
Why is that?
You should say: ‘It’s because they’re undeveloped.’
Undeveloped in what?

segs.p: Abhāvitattā catunnaṁ satipaṭṭhānānaṁ, abhāvitattā catunnaṁ sammappadhānānaṁ, abhāvitattā catunnaṁ iddhipādānaṁ, abhāvitattā pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ, abhāvitattā pañcannaṁ balānaṁ, abhāvitattā sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ, abhāvitattā ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa.
segs.e: Undeveloped in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, and the noble eightfold path.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā.
segs.e: Suppose there was a chicken with eight or ten or twelve eggs.

segs.p: Tānassu kukkuṭiyā na sammā adhisayitāni, na sammā pariseditāni, na sammā paribhāvitāni.
segs.e: But she had not properly sat on them to keep them warm and incubated.

segs.p: Kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyā evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: That chicken might wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata me kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṁ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjeyyun’ti,
segs.e: ‘If only my chicks could break out of the eggshell with their claws and beak and hatch safely!’

segs.p: atha kho abhabbāva te kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṁ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṁ.
segs.e: But they can’t break out and hatch safely.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathā hi pana, bhikkhave, kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā;
segs.e: Because that chicken with eight or ten or twelve eggs

segs.p: tāni kukkuṭiyā na sammā adhisayitāni, na sammā pariseditāni, na sammā paribhāvitāni.
segs.e: has not properly sat on them to keep them warm and incubated.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhāvanānuyogaṁ ananuyuttassa bhikkhuno viharato kiñcāpi evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: In the same way, when a mendicant is not committed to development, they might wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata me anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucceyyā’ti, atha khvassa neva anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: ‘If only my mind were freed from the defilements by not grasping!’ Even so, their mind is not freed from defilements by not grasping.
Why is that?
You should say: ‘It’s because they’re undeveloped.’
Undeveloped in what?

Undeveloped in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, and the noble eightfold path.

segs.p: Bhāvanānuyogaṁ anuyuttassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno viharato kiñcāpi na evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: When a mendicant is committed to development, they might not wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata me anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucceyyā’ti, atha khvassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: ‘If only my mind were freed from the defilements by not grasping!’ Even so, their mind is freed from defilements by not grasping.
Why is that?
You should say: ‘It’s because they are developed.’
Developed in what?

segs.p: Bhāvitattā catunnaṁ satipaṭṭhānānaṁ, bhāvitattā catunnaṁ sammappadhānānaṁ, bhāvitattā catunnaṁ iddhipādānaṁ, bhāvitattā pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ, bhāvitattā pañcannaṁ balānaṁ, bhāvitattā sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ, bhāvitattā ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa.
segs.e: Developed in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, and the noble eightfold path.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā.
segs.e: Suppose there was a chicken with eight or ten or twelve eggs.

segs.p: Tānassu kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitāni, sammā pariseditāni, sammā paribhāvitāni.
segs.e: And she properly sat on them to keep them warm and incubated.

segs.p: Kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyā na evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: That chicken might not wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata me kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṁ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjeyyun’ti,
segs.e: ‘If only my chicks could break out of the eggshell with their claws and beak and hatch safely!’

segs.p: atha kho bhabbāva te kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṁ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṁ.
segs.e: But still they can break out and hatch safely.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathā hi pana, bhikkhave, kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā;
segs.e: Because that chicken with eight or ten or twelve eggs

segs.p: tānassu kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitāni, sammā pariseditāni, sammā paribhāvitāni.
segs.e: properly sat on them to keep them warm and incubated.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhāvanānuyogaṁ anuyuttassa bhikkhuno viharato kiñcāpi na evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: In the same way, when a mendicant is committed to development, they might not wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata me anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucceyyā’ti, atha khvassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: ‘If only my mind were freed from the defilements by not grasping!’ Even so, their mind is freed from defilements by not grasping.
Why is that?
You should say: ‘It’s because they are developed.’
Developed in what?

segs.p: Bhāvitattā catunnaṁ satipaṭṭhānānaṁ …pe… bhāvitattā ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa.
segs.e: Developed in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, and the noble eightfold path.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, palagaṇḍassa vā palagaṇḍantevāsissa vā vāsijaṭe dissanteva aṅgulipadāni dissati aṅguṭṭhapadaṁ.
segs.e: Suppose a mason or their apprentice sees the marks of his fingers and thumb on the handle of his adze.

segs.p: No ca khvassa evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti:
segs.e: They don’t know

segs.p: ‘ettakaṁ vata me ajja vāsijaṭassa khīṇaṁ, ettakaṁ hiyyo, ettakaṁ pare’ti.
segs.e: how much of the handle was worn away today, how much yesterday, and how much previously.

segs.p: Atha khvassa khīṇe khīṇantveva ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: They just know what has been worn away.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhāvanānuyogaṁ anuyuttassa bhikkhuno viharato kiñcāpi na evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti:
segs.e: In the same way, when a mendicant is committed to development, they don’t know

segs.p: ‘ettakaṁ vata me ajja āsavānaṁ khīṇaṁ, ettakaṁ hiyyo, ettakaṁ pare’ti, atha khvassa khīṇe khīṇantveva ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: how much of the defilements were worn away today, how much yesterday, and how much previously. They just know what has been worn away.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sāmuddikāya nāvāya vettabandhanabaddhāya vassamāsāni udake pariyādāya hemantikena thalaṁ ukkhittāya vātātapaparetāni vettabandhanāni. Tāni pāvusakena meghena abhippavuṭṭhāni appakasireneva paṭippassambhanti pūtikāni bhavanti;
segs.e: Suppose there was a sea-faring ship bound together with ropes. For six months they deteriorated in the water. Then in the cold season it was hauled up on dry land, where the ropes were weathered by wind and sun. When the monsoon clouds soaked it with rain, the ropes would readily collapse and rot away.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhāvanānuyogaṁ anuyuttassa bhikkhuno viharato appakasireneva saṁyojanāni paṭippassambhanti pūtikāni bhavantī”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, when a mendicant is committed to development their fetters readily collapse and rot away.”

10. Flowers
The Perception of Impermanence
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Aniccasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā sabbaṁ kāmarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ rūparāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ bhavarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ avijjaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated it eliminates all desire for sensual pleasures, for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, and for rebirth in a future life. It eliminates all ignorance and eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, saradasamaye kassako mahānaṅgalena kasanto sabbāni mūlasantānakāni sampadālento kasati;
segs.e: In the autumn, a farmer ploughing with a large plough shears through all the root networks.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sabbaṁ kāmarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ rūparāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ bhavarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ avijjaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pabbajalāyako pabbajaṁ lāyitvā agge gahetvā odhunāti niddhunāti nicchoṭeti;
segs.e: A reed-cutter, having cut the reeds, grabs them at the top and shakes them down, shakes them about, and flails them about.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sabbaṁ kāmarāgaṁ pariyādiyati …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ambapiṇḍiyā vaṇṭacchinnāya yāni tattha ambāni vaṇṭapaṭibandhāni sabbāni tāni tadanvayāni bhavanti;
segs.e: When the stalk of a bunch of mangoes is cut, all the mangoes attached to the stalk will follow along.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā bhāvitā …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa yā kāci gopānasiyo sabbā tā kūṭaṅgamā kūṭaninnā kūṭasamosaraṇā, kūṭaṁ tāsaṁ aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: The rafters of a bungalow all lean to the peak, slope to the peak, and meet at the peak, so the peak is said to be the topmost of them all.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā bhāvitā …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci mūlagandhā kāḷānusārigandho tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: Of all kinds of fragrant root, spikenard is said to be the best.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci sāragandhā, lohitacandanaṁ tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: Of all kinds of fragrant heartwood, red sandalwood is said to be the best.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci pupphagandhā, vassikaṁ tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: Of all kinds of fragrant flower, jasmine is said to be the best.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci kuṭṭarājāno, sabbete rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā bhavanti, rājā tesaṁ cakkavatti aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: All lesser kings are vassals of a wheel-turning monarch, so the wheel-turning monarch is said to be the foremost of them all.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yā kāci tārakarūpānaṁ pabhā, sabbā tā candimappabhāya kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ, candappabhā tāsaṁ aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: The radiance of all the stars is not worth a sixteenth part of the moon’s radiance, so the moon’s radiance is said to be the best of them all.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nataṁ abbhussakkamāno, sabbaṁ ākāsagataṁ tamagataṁ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocate ca;
segs.e: In the autumn, the heavens are sunny and cloudless. And as the sun is rising to the firmament, having dispelled all the darkness of space, it shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sabbaṁ kāmarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ rūparāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ bhavarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ avijjaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated it eliminates all desire for sensual pleasures, for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, and for rebirth in a future life. It eliminates all ignorance and eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā kathaṁ bahulīkatā sabbaṁ kāmarāgaṁ pariyādiyati …pe… sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanati?
segs.e: And how is the perception of impermanence developed and cultivated so that … it eradicates all conceit ‘I am’?

segs.p: ‘Iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
segs.e: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.
Such is feeling …
Such is perception …
Such are choices …

segs.p: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti—
segs.e: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

segs.p: evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, aniccasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā sabbaṁ kāmarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ rūparāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ bhavarāgaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ avijjaṁ pariyādiyati, sabbaṁ asmimānaṁ samūhanatī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated so that it eliminates all desire for sensual pleasures, for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, and for rebirth in a future life. That’s how it eliminates all ignorance and eradicates all conceit ‘I am’.”

11. Ends
Ends
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, there are these four ends.
What four?

The end that is substantial reality, the end that is the origin of substantial reality, the end that is the cessation of substantial reality, and the end that is the practice that leads to the cessation of substantial reality.
And what is the end that is substantial reality?
It should be said: the five grasping aggregates.
What five?
That is, the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
This is called the end that is substantial reality.
And what is the end that is the origin of substantial reality?

segs.p: Yāyaṁ taṇhā ponobhavikā nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: It’s the craving that leads to future lives, mixed up with relishing and greed, taking pleasure there wherever it alights. That is,
craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for nonexistence.
This is called the end that is the origin of substantial reality.
And what is the end that is the cessation of substantial reality?

segs.p: Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo—
segs.e: It’s the fading away and cessation of that very same craving no residue left behind; giving it away, letting it go, releasing it, and not clinging to it.
This is called the end that is the cessation of substantial reality.
And what is the end that is the practice that leads to the cessation of substantial reality?
It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
This is called the end that is the practice that leads to the cessation of substantial reality.
These are the four ends.”

11. Ends
Suffering
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Dukkhañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi dukkhasamudayañca dukkhanirodhañca dukkhanirodhagāminiñca paṭipadaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.
Listen …
And what is suffering?
It should be said: the five grasping aggregates.
What five?
That is, the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
This is called suffering.
And what is the origin of suffering?

It’s the craving that leads to future lives, mixed up with relishing and greed, taking pleasure there wherever it alights. That is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for continued existence, and craving for nonexistence.
This is called the origin of suffering.
And what is the cessation of suffering?

segs.p: Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo—
segs.e: It’s the fading away and cessation of that very same craving with no residue left behind; giving it away, letting it go, releasing it, and not clinging to it.
This is called the cessation of suffering.
And what is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering?
It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
This is called the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.”

11. Ends
Should Be Completely Understood
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Pariññeyye ca, bhikkhave, dhamme desessāmi pariññañca pariññātāviñca puggalaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you the things that should be completely understood, complete understanding, and the individual who has completely understood.
Listen …
And what things should be completely understood?
Form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness.
These are called the things that should be completely understood.
And what is complete understanding?
The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.
This is called complete understanding.
And who is the individual who has completely understood?
It should be said: a perfected one,
the venerable of such name and such clan.
This is called the individual who has completely understood.”

“Mendicants, there are these five grasping aggregates.

That is, the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti …pe…
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape …

segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand …”

A Perfected One
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, there are these five grasping aggregates.
What five?
That is, the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti.
segs.e: A mendicant comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto”ti.
segs.e: Such a mendicant is called a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.”

At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Rūpe, bhikkhave, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form.

segs.p: Evaṁ taṁ rūpaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
segs.e: Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha.
segs.e: consciousness.

Ignorance
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe…
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘ignorance’.
What is ignorance?
And how is an ignoramus defined?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, assutavā puthujjano rūpaṁ nappajānāti, rūpasamudayaṁ nappajānāti, rūpanirodhaṁ nappajānāti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānāti;
segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
They don’t understand feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
This is called ignorance.
And this is how an ignoramus is defined.”

12. A Dhamma speaker
A Dhamma speaker
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of a ‘Dhamma speaker’.

segs.p: kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhammakathiko hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is a Dhamma speaker defined?”

segs.p: “Rūpassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: “Mendicant, if a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Rūpassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

segs.p: Rūpassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādāvimutto hoti, ‘diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they’re freed by not grasping by disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who has attained extinguishment in this very life’.
If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment with feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: viññāṇassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: consciousness, for its fading away and cessation, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Viññāṇassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

segs.p: Viññāṇassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādāvimutto hoti, ‘diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāyā”ti.

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī …pe… sappurisadhamme avinīto
segs.e: “Mendicants, take an unlearned ordinary person who has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano rūpabandhanabaddho santarabāhirabandhanabaddho atīradassī apāradassī, baddho jīyati baddho mīyati baddho asmā lokā paraṁ lokaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: They’re called an unlearned ordinary person who is bound to form, inside and out. They see neither the near shore nor the far shore. They’re born in bonds and die in bonds, and in bonds they go from this world to the next.

segs.p: Vedanaṁ attato samanupassati …pe… vedanāya vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: They regard feeling …

segs.e: A learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; na attani vā rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.

12. A Dhamma speaker
An Ethical Mendicant

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami …pe… etadavoca:
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita came out of retreat, went to Venerable Sāriputta, and said:

segs.p: “sīlavatāvuso, sāriputta, bhikkhunā katame dhammā yoniso manasikātabbā”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, what things should an ethical mendicant rationally apply the mind to?”

segs.p: “Sīlavatāvuso, koṭṭhika, bhikkhunā pañcupādānakkhandhā aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato yoniso manasi kātabbā.
segs.e: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, an ethical mendicant should rationally apply the mind to the five grasping aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.
What five?

segs.e: An ethical mendicant should rationally apply the mind to these five grasping aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati yaṁ sīlavā bhikkhu ime pañcupādānakkhandhe aniccato …pe… anattato yoniso manasi karonto sotāpattiphalaṁ sacchikareyyā”ti.
segs.e: It’s possible that an ethical mendicant who rationally applies the mind to the five grasping aggregates will realize the fruit of stream-entry.”

segs.p: “Sotāpannena panāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā katame dhammā yoniso manasi kātabbā”ti?
segs.e: “But Reverend Sāriputta, what things should a mendicant stream-enterer rationally apply the mind to?”

segs.p: “Sotāpannenapi kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, bhikkhunā ime pañcupādānakkhandhā aniccato …pe… anattato yoniso manasi kātabbā.

segs.e: It’s possible that a mendicant stream-enterer who rationally applies the mind to the five grasping aggregates will realize the fruit of once-return.”

segs.p: “Sakadāgāminā panāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā katame dhammā yoniso manasi kātabbā”ti?

segs.p: “Arahatā panāvuso sāriputta, katame dhammā yoniso manasi kātabbā”ti?
segs.e: “But Reverend Sāriputta, what things should a perfected one rationally apply the mind to?”

segs.p: “Arahatāpi kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, ime pañcupādānakkhandhe aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato yoniso manasi kātabbā.

13. Ignorance
Liable to Originate
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘ignorance’.
What is ignorance?
And how is an ignoramus defined?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, assutavā puthujjano samudayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘samudayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti;
segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t truly understand form, which is liable to originate, as form which is liable to originate.
They don’t truly understand form, which is liable to vanish, as form which is liable to vanish.
They don’t truly understand form, which is liable to originate and vanish, as form which is liable to originate and vanish.
They don’t truly understand feeling …
perception …

consciousness, which is liable to originate, as consciousness which is liable to originate.
They don’t truly understand consciousness, which is liable to vanish, as consciousness which is liable to vanish.
They don’t truly understand consciousness, which is liable to originate and vanish, as consciousness which is liable to originate and vanish.
This is called ignorance.
And this is how an ignoramus is defined.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the mendicant said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘knowledge’.

segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when a learned noble disciple truly understands form, which is liable to originate, as form which is liable to originate.

Burning Chaff
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, kukkuḷaṁ, vedanā kukkuḷā, saññā kukkuḷā, saṅkhārā kukkuḷā, viññāṇaṁ kukkuḷaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are burning chaff.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

“Mendicants, when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith, this is what’s in line with the teaching.

segs.p: yaṁ rūpe nibbidābahulo vihareyya. Vedanāya …pe… saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe nibbidābahulo vihareyya.
segs.e: They should live full of disillusionment for form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Yo rūpe nibbidābahulo viharanto, vedanāya … saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe nibbidābahulo viharanto rūpaṁ parijānāti, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ parijānāti;
segs.e: Living in this way, they completely understand form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: so rūpaṁ parijānaṁ vedanaṁ parijānaṁ saññaṁ parijānaṁ saṅkhāre parijānaṁ viññāṇaṁ parijānaṁ parimuccati rūpamhā, parimuccati vedanāya, parimuccati saññāya, parimuccati saṅkhārehi, parimuccati viññāṇamhā, parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi; ‘parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: Completely understanding form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness, they’re freed from these things. They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re freed from suffering, I say.”

segs.p: “Kismiṁ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṁ upādāya uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhan”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what, do pleasure and pain arise in oneself?”
“Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

segs.p: “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati rūpaṁ upādāya uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: “When form exists, because of grasping form, pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

segs.e: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would pleasure and pain arise in oneself?”

15. Views
With Ānanda
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā …pe… bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”
“What do you think, Ānanda?
Is form permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
